crux.for_the_english: he must never become quaint Cockney or stage-Japanese. Use dropped, run-on, self-interrupting colloquial syntax, repetitions and verbal tics in place of the sentence-ending な and the self-deprecating でげす forms, and let the dignity show through competence and generosity, not through making his grammar more respectable.
crux.point: keep Nekohachi's patter as work, not local colour
crux.why: His banter on the tram in p2-p10 is not decoration before the serious part begins; it is the act itself, carried on in public because passengers have become an audience and a comeback is professionally compulsory. Again at the meeting he tests jokes, misapplies the borrowed word "situation" (p67-p69), apologises, recovers, and feels the flatness when は、は、は does not come (p63). If English tidies this into witty repartee it ennobles him; if it renders it as broad dialect comedy it does to him exactly what his audiences do.

crux.for_the_english: do not iron out the long, associative sentences in which cabbages, a bath, a fee and a son succeed one another, and do not cut the lists. Keep the repetitions - animals, vegetables, children, money - as repetitions: they are Berman's networks, the web the story is made of, not redundancy to be varied away.
crux.point: keep the ramble, because the ramble is the consciousness
crux.why: The narration stays glued to Nekohachi's mind, and that mind does not proceed: on the tram it slides from a heckle to why a comedian must not laugh, to protecting a voice he does not drink for, to caterpillars in a ditch and cutworms that, like thieves and like himself, work only at night (p10-p14). The garden returns at every pressure point (p20, p31-p33, p100, p158, p172-p173) and is still what he offers the departing gentlemen at his own gate (p182). A fluent version that breaks this into themed paragraphs, or clarifies the transitions, has rationalised away the man.

crux.for_the_english: keep the embedded summary flat and a little long-winded, keep its pathos unlyrical, and keep Nekohachi's interventions in his own terms (a father should not let the child see it) rather than translating them into the group's critical vocabulary. Let the reader feel the identification before Nekohachi names 悲哀 for himself.
crux.point: let 'The Tiger' stay a clumsy paraphrase, not a set piece
crux.why: Half the story is a second-hand retelling of Kume's tale of a comic actor cast as a tiger whose child finds him weeping in the wings (p48-p90). It would be easy to polish this into a moving story-within-the-story. In the text it arrives as reported talk, interrupted, jargon-dusted (シチュエイション, バック), and judged thin by everyone present. Its power for Nekohachi is precisely that this mediocre fiction has got his life: four sons, a gifted twelve-year-old he has moved to the suburbs to keep away from the yose (p50, p93-p95). Prettify the paraphrase and his response looks disproportionate; sentimentalise his response and the literati's cool verdict loses its sting.

reading.head_on_cruxes: They name different things, not the same thing in different words: Option 0 makes the crux the preservation of Nekohachi's rambling, repetitious, professionally performed consciousness and the deliberate flatness of the embedded paraphrase, while Option 1 makes it the unblended clash of his English with the literati's and the refusal to resolve sorrow against performance. Because that difference will recur in register, paragraphing, the retelling and the ending, and being wrong about which governs would be expensive, this goes up as a fork.

open_questions.question: How far to take Nekohachi's borrowed critical words? He picks up シチュエイション and uses it to mean something like a fix, then perhaps 'compromise' (p67-p69), asks after a novel's 落ち as if it were a rakugo punchline (p82), and hears バック/ハイケイ and こんにゃく問答 as pure sound (p118). Keeping the English words 'situation' and 'background' preserves the joke that he is mouthing English; explaining his misunderstandings in the text would clarify what the story leaves for the reader to infer.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is where the class gap is audible. Over-explanation makes him stupid, under-explanation makes the passages merely opaque, and either choice decides how much the reader laughs at him rather than with him.

open_questions.question: What to do with the blanked names ○○○様 and ○○家 (p155, p159, p168)? The blanks are in the source: discretion about aristocratic patrons, performed in the telling. Silently filling, footnoting speculative identities, or smoothing them into 'a certain lord' would each change the effect; the blank itself is Nekohachi showing he knows how to behave in great houses.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The blanks mark the exact border between his world and the one that summons carriages for him. They are also part of his boasting: he has been to houses whose names must be withheld.

open_questions.question: How straight to play the revelation that Kume anonymously savaged his own story in a review (p103), which instantly converts Nekohachi into Kume's admirer (p104)? The group reads it as frivolity; Nekohachi reads it as 茶気, a performer's trick he recognises, and concludes the audience decides (p107-p108).
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the one moment his professional judgement and the literati's may be pointing, from opposite sides, at the same thing. Playing it as simple irony rebukes him; playing it as simple insight rebukes them.

open_questions.question: Is the ending's humility (p185) a genuine change of heart, a mood of one in the morning that will not survive breakfast, or the last performance of the night, given to himself? He wants to embrace the tiger and weep (p175), is ashamed of his own relief at two yen (p177), and goes home resolved to make his wife taste an entertainer's sorrow (p188).
open_questions.why_it_matters: An English ending that resolves into renunciation or redemption betrays the text; so does one that undercuts him with open irony. The temperature of the last page is an editorial fork the reading cannot settle.

reading.reading:
The crux of 『猫八』 is a man hearing his own life told back to him as somebody else's mediocre fiction, and being unable to say so in any language the room will accept. Nekohachi is a yose mimic, half-crippled by rheumatism for over a decade, who earns his living imitating cats fighting, birds, insects and latterly aeroplanes, and who has moved his family to an inconvenient suburb precisely so that his gifted twelve-year-old son will not watch him do it and will not become a second Nekohachi (p50, p95). Taken by the patron Takami to a writers' study group, he listens to a flat paraphrase of Kume's 「虎」, about a comic actor cast as a tiger, proud of the applause, and found after the curtain by his small son, crying in the costume: "the tiger and the human child wept together for a while in the shadow of the dark scenery" (p87). Everyone present agrees the piece is shallow, deft, thin in background. Nekohachi sits with one hand on the tatami and thinks it is about him. A translation stands or falls on whether that recognition lands without ever being upgraded into insight: he does not achieve self-knowledge in the story, he achieves a feeling - 悲哀, a word he has literally just learned from the man across the room (p56-p57) - and he carries it home past the sleeping tenement like something he has been paid in.

Everything follows from keeping the two registers unmerged. Nekohachi's spoken voice is Edo working patter: ingratiating, self-deprecating, built on な and でげす, forever turning a slight into a routine - the heckler on the tram must be answered because the other passengers have become an audience (p5-p10), the fat acquaintance must be greeted with 大山大将 and a lie about another engagement to save face (p23-p26), a lord's carriage must be met by borrowing a kimono from the blacksmith's wife and pretending to come back from the bath (p159). This is not colour; it is labour, and it is also evasion. Against it stands the literati's talk, abstract, loanworded and cool: シチュエイション, バック, 現実主義, 具体的, personality as the backing of a work (p103-p117). Nekohachi understands none of the terms and most of the substance. He thinks "situation" may mean a tight spot, which for him it does: he is はめられて, fitted into the patrons' favour until he can no longer move (p53). The translation must let the reader hear that he is misusing their words and meaning something truer with them, without a narrator stepping in to award him the point. Equally, the gentlemen must not be flattened into villains. They are mildly kind, mildly bored, they feed him餅菓子 instead of the drink he refuses, the host's wife talks gardens and children with him (p119-p120), Takami quietly presses two yen on him outside (p176) - and three of them walk out in the middle of the most honest story he ever tells (p161). Condescension here is structural, not snarling, and English that gives them sneers, or gives him a rebuttal, destroys it.

The narration is the third voice and the treacherous one, because it keeps slipping into Nekohachi's own idiom and self-justifications: the long tram reverie that moves from why a comedian must not laugh, to the voice he protects by not drinking, to green caterpillars shaken into a ditch and stamped on (p10-p13); the sudden boilerplate of Edo pride, no money kept overnight, born in Asakusa to a geisha mother (p158), set down right beside the admission that he beats his wife for trying to save (p175). The narrator neither endorses nor corrects any of this. That evenness is what a fluent draft will most want to fix, by making the interior passages lyrical where the story turns sad and brisk where it is comic. Resist it. The prose should stay dogged, repetitive and faintly garrulous even at p175, when he wants, in hiding, to embrace the tiger and weep for a while: the bathos is the emotion, and ennobling it into a climax would be the exact falsification the story is about.

Against the stage the text sets the allotment, and it must be translated as seriously as the tiger. Digging a ditch along the rows so the caterpillars roll in (p12), watching for cutworms that work nights as he does (p13), worrying on the tram home that two or three seedlings' roots will be cut before he gets back (p20), the surplus cucumbers and aubergines he gives away (p11, p182): this is the one place he is competent without being laughed at, and the one generosity nobody applauds. Note that he ends the evening not with a resolution to quit - he does wish, at p177, that he could stop tomorrow - but by advertising his vegetables to the departing writers at his own dark gate, and planning to make his wife taste what he has felt (p182-p188). The shape is a long evening that changes nothing except the temperature of a man's self-pity, and translations that sharpen it into an arc of awakening will have imported the 落ち he himself kept asking for and was laughed at for expecting (p82-p85).

Repetitions are load-bearing throughout: the animal catalogue that runs from tiger, monkey and pig (p179) through his frog-origin story (p141-p145) to the firefly and the colic-worm he cannot imitate and blusters about (p147-p153); the children and the dreaded second Nekohachi; the fee that must never be named and is always on his mind (p171, p175-p177); the 気違いか猫八のような化け物 of the opening joke (p6), madmen and monsters as the only residents of Sugamo, which the whole story quietly tests. Keep them unvaried. Keep his set-pieces - the caged nightingale, the valley-crossing, the mating cranes, the earthworm research that got him taken for a burglar (p62, p124-p130) - as performance, with the room's inadequate laughter left inadequate. And keep the unglamorous furniture: Kōdan Club magazine, the gas lamp he has petitioned to advertise himself with (p186), the leftover cakes in his pocket with the borrowed magazines. This is a Taishō naturalist story whose pity works by inventory, not by statement.

second_crux.for_the_english: Keep two audible Englishes unblended: Nekohachi in a working, comic, self-interrupting stage patter full of swallowed retorts and asides, the writers in flat, borrowed critical abstraction; never polish either into the same literary fluency, and let the reader feel when neither fully understands the other.
second_crux.point: The collision of languages is the action: close third-person narration saturated with Nekohachi's Edokko yose patter (でげす, な, self-deprecating jokes, internal 洒落 he performs even to himself) set against the literati's imported jargon (シチュエイション, バック, 現実主義/具体) that he literally cannot parse. He is never off stage—he swallows '小奈良の小大仏' (p8), turns a tram ride into a 高座 (p5-9), negotiates every humiliation as a gag—while they study that very compulsion as '悲哀' in Kume's '虎'.
second_crux.why: Strip the register gap and the plot (a mimic taken to a research society) has no tension left: his mishearings of 'situation' as a predicament he is trapped in (p53), his gratitude at being quoted back as criticism (p79-82), and his final triumph in performance (p124-136) all only register because we hear him thinking and speaking in a different tongue from theirs.

second_crux.for_the_english: Hold the double exposure in the English: render his self-recognitions and the closing humility straight, without irony markers, ennoblement, or a softened/resolved ending, so the reader—not the prose—decides how much is insight and how much is act.
second_crux.point: The mirrored tiger must stay unresolved: Nekohachi condemns Fukai for letting his child see the debasing role (p91-95) and has moved to the suburbs to hide his own, yet eagerly performs, fishes for praise and a fee (p171-177), and misreads Kume's anonymous self-denunciation as proof Kume is a wit after his own heart (p103-110). The text itself flags that even his grief-stricken face is partly exaggeration he half-knows about (p91), and ends not in renunciation—he plans to retell the novel to his wife (p188)—but in a 'rare' humble, human feeling (p185) alongside gas-lamp advertising and the night's two coins.
second_crux.why: If the translation settles him as either dignified artist-victim (the literati's '悲哀' made true) or comic butt the reader pities from above, it picks the side the story refuses: his sorrow is real and performed at once, his pride in hiding the act from his sons coexists with delight that '例の猫八' is known (p37-39), and that undecidability is what the whole mirrored structure was built to produce.

voice_takes.label: close, warm, and performed - the house recommendation
voice_takes.line: Narration in plain, slightly long-winded English that keeps slipping into Nekohachi's own turn of phrase without quotation marks or apology; it reports his self-flatteries (Edo-born, money never kept overnight) in the same tone as his seedlings, and never steps back to judge either. Nekohachi himself in dropped, wheedling, run-on speech, all apologies and 'now, look here' and sentence-final appeals for agreement, quickening into pure act - sound-words, animal cries, abrupt changes of face - when he performs; his seriousness should keep breaking the patter rather than replacing it. The literati in complete, abstract, faintly bored sentences, polysyllabic where he is monosyllabic, kind in the way of people who will not be there at the end of the sentence. Takami a register between: clubbable, easy, the only man who speaks both languages. Wrong for this take: dialect spelling, music-hall Cockney, 'gee' and 'ain't' folksiness, or any lyric lift at the tiger's climax - the moment the English gets beautiful, it has joined the study group against him.

voice_takes.label: drier and more naturalist
voice_takes.line: Narration flatter and cooler, closer to reportage, letting the inventories of the tenement, the allotment and the evening's talk accumulate without warmth, so that Nekohachi's bursts of patter stand out as noise he makes against a quiet world. His speech still colloquial but less lovable - more repetitive, more importunate - and the literati barely differentiated from one another, a single murmur of educated dismissal. This take risks seeming to side with the room, but it honours Iwano's naturalism and makes the final walk home colder and less consoling. Wrong for it: any softening of the wife-beating admission or the fee anxiety, which this take needs unglossed to work.

voice_takes.label: more theatrical, playing the act
voice_takes.line: Narration keeps pace with a performer thinking: quicker cuts, jokes left to land or die in the spacing, the animal imitations given real stage room with their onomatopoeia carried over, and the study-group scenes played almost as dialogue in a play, Nekohachi a comic turn among tragedians. His origin story on the Yoshiwara embankment becomes the bravura centre it is in his own mind. This take is the most readable aloud and the most dangerous: it flatters exactly the gift the story is examining, and will need discipline to keep the garden passages, the walkouts and the two yen as heavy as the applause. Wrong for it: punchlines sharpened beyond the source, or pathos borrowed back from the tiger to pay for the comedy.

casual.ja: 「例のは気に入りました、な、わたくしも多少は知られた芸人ですから。あなたがたのような偉い文士方の前へ出ましても、な、その、そうおじ気が出ないのは仕合せです」こう言ってじろりと一座を見わたすと、無邪気に笑ったものもあるし、別に感触を害しているようなものもないらしいので、こちらの洒落を皆寛大に理解してくれる人々だと分った。が、なお念のためにもッと分らせておくつもりで、「ただし前もってお断わりしておきますが、わたくしはリョウマチのために人様のようにはからだが利きません。したがって、こうわざと畏まってますように見えるのもそのためでげして、あながち諸君を怖がってるわけではございません」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "ha, ha, ha" came, so he felt safe for a start, and thinking they were his now he shut his mouth for a while.

casual.en: To the question, "What sort of story is it?" the host answered, "I only glanced through it because he asked me by postcard to bring it up — thin if you call it thin, but neatly put together at its low level. The author can hardly have demanded much of himself, so for that author it will do well enough, I suppose — 'Tiger' is the part the hero, a comic actor, has been cast to play. To quote the original, this actor 'had a child already eight years old. And the child had trodden his first stage last year and had before him a future as a shinpa actor like him, no, more proper than him. He thought he would never make the child a comic.'"
casual.ja: 「どんな筋なんでしょう」という問いに主人は答えて、
casual.label: house-checked

casual.ja: 「僕もその人が問題にしてくれろと、ハガキで言ってきてあったのでちょッと読んでおいただけなのですが、――浅薄と言えば浅薄な物だが、低い程度で器用には纒まってると思う。作者にもそう深い要求がなかったのだろうから、あの作者としてはあれでもいいのでしょうが――虎とは作の主人公なる三枚目俳優が扮することになった役目です。この俳優には、原文を引くと、『もう、八歳になる子があった。そしてその子は去年初舞台を踏んで彼と同じく否、彼よりももッと正式な、新派俳優になる未来をもっていた。彼はその子をけっして三枚目にはしたくないと思った』」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "…" Hearing this reading, Nekohachi felt he had walked into an awful place. He knew himself that this was a bit of an overblown thought, and yet it sounded just as if they were talking about himself. He had four boys, the eldest fourteen in first year of higher primary, the next twelve in fifth year of elementary, both doing well and both monitors. This twelve year old was good at mimicking his father, and had an art even beyond his father's, but for all that he would not make him a second Nekohachi. No, it was just so as not to let the children see their father mimicking cat fights and animal voices and coaxing good humour out of the customers from up on the koza that he had long ago gone out of his way to choose this inconvenient suburb to live in. Cat turned to tiger, there was no great difference in that.
casual.ja: 「………」この本読みを聴いて猫八はえらいところへ飛びこんできたものだと思われた。この思いは自分でも少しおおげさな考えだとは承知しながら、まるで自分の事を言われているようであった。自分には男の子が四人あって、総領は十四で高等一年、次ぎは十二で尋常五年、いずれも出来がよくて級長をしている。この十二のが父親の真似が上手で、しかも父親以上の芸を持ってるが、それでも第二の猫八にはしたくないのである。否、父親が猫の喧嘩や動物の声を真似して、高座のうえから客の機嫌を取ってるところを子供に見せたくないためにこそ、早くからわざわざこんな不便な郊外を選んで住んでるのだ。猫が虎に変っても、そこにたいした相違はない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "The part handed him was just the one part of the tiger." What the host was reading seemed to be the text of the story itself. "Not a man's name. Just the one part dressed up as a real beast of a tiger. He had even taken the byname of animal actor, so what wonder now to be handed the tiger to play. And yet he felt a little sad. Used to it as he long was, profession as he thought it, teasing as he knew it to be, he felt the human inside him being made a fool of, and even felt a little angry. The hero is in that sort of *situation*."
casual.ja: 「彼の振られた役というのは、ただ虎の一役だッた」主人が読んでるのはその小説の本文らしかった。「人の名ではない。ほんとのけだ物の虎に扮する一役だけだッた。動物役者という異名をさえ取っていたので、今さら虎の役を振られたとて、それが何の不思議であろう。けれども、ちょッと悲しく感じた。長年馴れてきていながら、職業だと思っていながら、どうせ茶化しているのだとは思いながら、自分の中なる人間がばかにされてるような気がして、ちょッと腹立たしくさえ思ったというようなシチュエイションにある主人公です」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Quite deftly the point the author was aiming at holds together throughout," put in the man with the face like Tenjin-sama, in an earnest tone.
casual.ja: 「なかなか器用には作者の狙ったところは一貫しています」と、天神さまみたような顔つきの人が熱心な口調で口を出した。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "…" The English word situation the host had just used stayed in Nekohachi's ears, and he took it to mean something like a painful fix you get caught in. And he himself was in fact fitted into his customers' favour, and had gone and fitted himself right into it, till he was in the state he was in now where he could move neither one way nor the other, so he joked it to himself, quiet. But down underneath he felt the hateful part of the performer's trade all the more.
casual.ja: 「………」猫八には、今主人が言ったシチュエイションという英語が耳に残って、苦しいはめといったような意味の言葉ではないかしらんと想像された。そして自分は実際にお客様方の御贔負についはめられて、それに自分もついはまりこみ、とうとう二進も三進も動けない今の身分になってるのだとひそかに洒落れてみた。が、その心の奥ではますます芸人のいやなことを感じた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "There is the place where the leader points it out, eh, says that is just Fukai-kun's fitted part," said the priest-like one, close-cropped, with bumps rising fore and aft like a mountain range, the knowing face.
casual.ja: 「座長がそりゃア深井君のはまり役だと指摘するところがあります、ね」と、五分刈りあたまの前後へむッくり山脈のできた善智識顔の坊さんらしいのが言った。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "And then they tell him the whole act will be eaten clean up by Fukai-kun's tiger, and such," the host went on, "and he got that much proud again even. But being the tiger, with no lines to say, there was no call to turn up for rehearsals even. Glad to make use of the day when the child begged to go to Ueno Zoo, he says, well then shall I show you the much talked of hippo, while in truth he means to go and study how a tiger looks. Then on the way, in the tram, he meets a theatre critic, and is asked where he is off to, so he answers, truth to tell, to the zoo to show the child the much talked of hippo, but the sharp critic has him marked, that is a lie, I have heard it already, it is the tiger really."
casual.ja: 「それから他のものにもその幕はすッかり深井君の虎に喰われてしまうというようなことを言われて」と、主人は言葉を進めた、「彼はいくらかまた得意にさえなった。けれども、虎だから、台辞を言うことがないので稽古にも出る必要がない。その日を利用して子供は上野の動物園へ行ってくれろと言うのを幸い、じゃア近ごろ評判の河馬でも見せてやろうかと言って、その実、自分は虎の様子をでも研究してくるつもりになった。すると、途中、電車のうちである劇評家に出会い、どこへ行くのだと尋ねられたので、じつは、子供に大評判の河馬を見せに動物園までと答えたが、機敏な劇評家からそりゃア嘘だろう、もう聴いてるよ、じつは虎だろうと目星をさされた」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "There is a kind of sorrow comes out in a bit like that too," said the Tenjin-sama man.
casual.ja: 「そういうところにも一種の悲哀は出ています」と、天神さまが言った。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "…" Nekohachi opened his eyes wide as if for the first time on hearing the word sorrow. It seemed to him more and more as if his own affair had been taken and remade and dug into. With his right hand stuck on the tatami and his left laid on the folded hand towel on his knee, admiring at how human feeling falls to the same place whoever feels it, he leaned his head a little back where he sat sideways and said, "I see! To an unlearned one like me a novel seemed a slapdash made-up thing with eight hundred lies strung together in it — though that may have been rude from the start to Sensei gentlemen like yourselves — but to hear it now, sure enough it aims at the true thing, it does, eh"
casual.ja: 「………」猫八は悲哀という言葉を聴いて、今さらのように目を見張った。ますます自分のことでも作り換えて、うがってあるように思えたからである。右の手を畳に突いて、左りの手を膝の上にある畳んだ手拭いの上に置いてたのだが、人情というものは誰れが感じても結局こう同じところに落ちるのかと感心して、その横坐わりのままあたまを少し後ろへ反らせて「なるほど！　わたくしのような無学のものには小説なんかはいい加減に作り事を書いて、うそ八百を並べてあるものと思っておりましたが、――もっともこれはお歴々の先生方には初めから失礼であったかもしれませんが――今伺ってみますと、なるほど本統のことを狙ってあるものでげす、な」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Present-day novels are all like that, of course," the Tenjin-sama man answered, sounding a little angry. "We are different novelists from novelists who write lies and rest satisfied with it!"
casual.ja: 「今の小説はむろん皆そうだよ」例のは少し怒ったように答えた。「うそを書いて満足している小説家とは吾々は小説家が違います！」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Fu, fun," went the knowledge-face man, laughing through his nose.
casual.ja: 「ふ、ふん」と鼻で笑うのは智識がおであった。

casual.en: "How you do flare up," said the very near-sighted-looking man, smiling as he teased him.

casual.en: "I am not flaring up in particular, only there are plenty of fools in the world who take slapdash popular novels like Hekirurien's or Tokutomi Roka's for the fine standard and pass low, vulgar criticism."
casual.ja: 「別に憤慨しているのではないけれど、世間にはよくばか者があって、碧瑠璃園や徳富蘆花のようないい加減な通俗小説をえい方の標準にして俗悪な批評をするものが多いから」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Terribly sorry, I am sure," Nekohachi said, keeping a straight face and dipping his head a little, and they all laughed. But this time that alone left him feeling unsatisfied, so he offered up one joke. "I for my part have never yet met a theatre critic in the course of my own researches, no, but once, to study the cry of the earthworm, I squatted up all night in the woods by the Veterans' Home over there, and they took me for a thief and a detective challenged me, he did, eh."
casual.ja: 「どうもすみません」猫八はすました顔でちょッと頭を下げたので、皆が笑った。が、それだけでは今度は自分が満足できないような気になって、一つ冗談を言った。「わたくしは、しかし研究の途中でまだ劇評家にはお会いしたことがございませんが、ある時、蚯蚓の啼き声を研究するために、あの、そこの廃兵院の森に夜明しをしてしゃがんでおりましたら、泥棒と見誤られて刑事に誰何されたことがございます」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That too, you know, is the result of a kind of sorrow or earnestness," was all the explanation Tenjin-sama gave, and from no one else came any ha, ha, ha.
casual.ja: 「それも、君、一種の悲哀かまじめかの結果だよ」という天神様の説明があっただけで、別に誰からも、は、は、はッとは来なかった。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "…" Nekohachi felt the wind taken clean out of him, against all expectation. And for the first time it struck him that these were not his customers. As an entertainer he might make people cry or laugh, but he had no room left to cry or laugh himself. These people, though, were a cut above even that, for they seemed to study even the feeling of an entertainer himself who makes people cry or laugh and cannot cry or laugh himself. They were specialists in that line, right enough. At this rate an honest humility rose in him to take off his helmet cleanly and own himself beaten, and he asked, "And what did the actor do after that?" What he wanted to know most was about the child. All the same he had quite made up his mind the fall would be that he pleaded the part unworthy and did not go on the stage, or that at least he did not let the child come to the theatre.
casual.ja: 「………」猫八は予期に反して、がッくり調子抜けがした。そして初めて思い及んだのであるが、これは自分のお客ではない。自分は芸人として人を泣かせたり笑わせたりしても、自分の泣いたり笑ったりする余地を持たない。ところが、この人々はまた自分らよりも一段うわ手で、人を泣かせたり笑わせたりする芸人その物の自分では泣いたり笑ったりできないその心持ちまでも研究しているらしい。さすがはその方の専門家たちだろう。これじゃア自分は潔く兜を脱ごうという正直な謙遜心を起して、「そうしてその俳優はそれからどういたしました」と尋ねてみた。おもに子供との関係を知りたかったのである。それでも、たぶん、役不足を言って舞台に出なかったとか、子供だけは芝居へ見に来させなかったとかいうのが落ちだろうとたかをくくっていた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.ja: 三
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Just look. You've made a clean confession, haven't you, but if you want to see a tiger you needn't go all the way to the zoo — give anyone a litre or two and he'll turn into one, eh? — Why, shall we go and see that tiger over there? — That won't do. I can't shake this little one off, you see, and he looked back at the child again. There's a passage like that too," the host went on, still with an eye on the book. And everyone forgot Nekohachi and the rest and bent their hearts toward the tiger, but to Nekohachi that tiger was like himself. "For foolishness, Yui's part is much the same. Rather your single tiger part may be the honour, with the popularity gathering on the tiger alone, you know — thinking so I mean to do all I can with all my might, you know — Yes indeed, we for our part are rather counting on your tiger — Much obliged, and Fukai smiled wryly and yet was not a little comforted in his heart."
casual.ja: 「そうれ見たまえ。みごとに白状に及んだじゃないかね、しかし虎を見たいんならわざわざ動物園まで行くにも及ぶまいぜ。――一二升飲ませれゃ誰だってなりますが？――どうだい、そッちの虎を見に行こうじゃないか？――そいつアいけません。何しろこいつを撒くわけには行きませんからね、と彼はまた子供をかえりみた。というところもあるのだが」と、主人はなお本を見い見い語って行った。そして皆が猫八などのいるのを忘れて虎の方へ心を傾けたが、猫八にはその虎が自分のようであった。「ばかさ加減を言えば由井の役だッて同じようなものさ。むしろ君の虎一役が名誉かもしれんぜ、人気が虎の一身に集まったりして、ね。――そう思ってわたくしも一生懸命やるだけはやるつもりなんですが、ね。――そうとも、僕たちだッてむしろ君の虎に期待しているよ。――恐れ入ります、と深井は苦笑をしながらも、内心少からず慰められた」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That won't do, eh," Nekohachi said, screwing up his face, "to do that situation in a place like that!"
casual.ja: 「いけません、な」と、猫八は顔を顰めてみせながら、「そんなところで例のシチュエイションをやっては！」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "ufu, fu," a stylish little laugh was heard.
casual.ja: 「うふ、ふ」と、乙な笑いが聞えた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Before gentlemen like you, for the likes of me to use cheeky English may have been a mistake —" He had thought better of it that this English might come to what they call compromise, but, "anyhow, if that actor they call Fukai lets the critic's puffing talk the decent human thought he had managed to hold in that case clean away, and goes carelessly getting into the swing again, that will be trouble, eh."
casual.ja: 「先生がたの前で、わたくし風情が、生意気な英語の使い方をしたのは間違ってるか存じませんが――」この英語はいわゆる妥協ということに当るのではないかと思いなおしたのだが、「とにかく、その深井とかいう俳優がその場合にせっかく持った真人間らしい考えを、劇評家の煽てでなくさせてしまい、うかうかとまた調子づいて行っちゃア困ります、な」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "But that is just what makes it interesting, in a way —" the host said.
casual.ja: 「ところが、そうであるからかえっておもしろくもあるのだが――」と、主人は言った。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "But as for me, a thing like that —" he said, turning earnest as if to show he was not fool enough for that, but neither the host nor any of the rest lent him an ear.
casual.ja: 「しかしわたくしならそんなことは」と、彼は自分をそんなばかでもないと弁護するように熱心じみたが、主人ばかりでなく皆も耳をかたむけてくれなかった。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "He went to the zoo and did no more than watch the tiger sitting still and yawning, and yet he came home thinking he had got the tiger's feelings better, somehow, than a handsome lover's feelings. When the first day came and the sewn-up tiger came onto the stage and yawned, at that alone there were cries of Fukai, Fukai! from the gallery, and he grew not a little proud. And at the fall of the curtain, when he leapt upon the heroine of the play, gallery first and the whole house with it gave him a great burst of applause."
casual.ja: 「動物園に行って虎のじッとしているところや欠伸をしたのを見ただけでも、彼はとにかく色男の気持ちよりも虎の気持ちをよく分ったと思って帰宅した。いよいよ初日が来て、縫いぐるみの虎が舞台に出て欠伸をすると、それだけでも大向うから深井、深井！　と呼ぶ声がかかったので、すくなからず得意になった。そしてその幕切れのところで劇の女主人公に躍りかかると、大向うを初めとして諸見物の大喝采を得た」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Isn't that making fools of people?" It was the words of the much younger man, speaking for the first time.
casual.ja: 「人をばかにしているじゃアありませんか？」これは初めて口に出すずッと若い人の言葉であった。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That is making a fool of people, right enough," Tenjin-sama put in too, laughing this time.
casual.ja: 「そりゃ人をばかにしたもの、さ」と、天神さまも今度は笑いながら口出しをした。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: A grudge rose in Nekohachi too about the way customers treat him on the kōza, enough to make him want to have his say. "From where I stand, it is the spectators he is making fools of, for getting delighted over trifles, and I daresay he is feeling for the actor himself, eh — spectators are the same as yose customers, you know."
casual.ja: 「………」猫八もまた何か言ってみたくなったほど高座で受けるお客からの待遇に対する不平が浮んでいた。「そりゃア、わたくしから見ますと、つまらないことを嬉しがる見物人の事をばかにしているのでごぜいまして、たぶんその俳優の本人には同情していてくれてるのでげしょう、な――見物なんて、寄席のお客も同様でげすから」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Now, about that," Takami-san put in his first question with a mild look, "is it a work where the author is being ironical — I have not read a scrap of it, so I can hardly have an opinion — but to go by what I have just heard?"
casual.ja: 「いったい、それは」と、高見さんは穏かな顔つきで初めて質問を出した、「作者が皮肉を言ってる作でしょうか――僕はさッぱり読んでいませんから、意見のあろうはずはないのですが、――今、聴いたところをもってみれば？」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It is irony, to be sure," the knowledge-face man answered in a set-piece tone, "the question is whether the author can be satisfied with irony of so shallow a degree."
casual.ja: 「皮肉には違いないのですが」と、知識がおが切り口上で答えた、「こんな浅薄な程度の皮肉でも作者が満足できるかどうかが問題でしょう」
casual.label: house-checked

He looks back in surprise and finds his own child crying, child as he is, at the foolish part his father has played. He too cannot help crying, now at last. And then, 'the tiger and the human child wept together for a while in the shadow of the dark background,' that is how it ends."

casual.en: "…" Nekohachi made a show of opening his eyes wide, as if thunderstruck, when he came to hear of this last business of weeping together. He could not say he did not know himself that this too was a face put on and exaggerated on purpose, and yet at the same time, before he knew it, what was always kept hidden in the bottom of his heart seemed to have come out upon his face, for the grief over his own trade and the wavering over whether to make his second son into a second Nekohachi had been coaxed out together at once. He tried not to show people a face so ill-suited to his comic trade, but the harder he tried the less the face itself would obey him, quite the other way, and if he saw it in a mirror he thought it must look like a blubbering face. But without patching it up any more, plainly, "Well, I am impressed," he showed his respect as if the story were the very work of the company present. "I've got the same sort of sorrow myself, and it truly struck home, it did, eh. But if I too may be allowed the one, what you gentlemen would call a criticism, this Fukai playing a part against his own wish and letting his child see it, that I think was a grave mistake, eh?"

Then straight on the voices of the pine cricket, the bell cricket, the kutsuwamushi. Then crow, skylark, quail. With his joined lips pushed flat out to the front, the voice of the mole-cricket. Saying it might be a bother to the neighbours quieted to sleep by now, the male crane and the female crane told apart in the cry. The grass lark's voice too he let them hear.
casual.ja: 「今のは籠の中での鶯ですが、今度は谷わたり」けきょ、けきょ、けきょ、ほうほけきょう！　それから引き続いて松虫、鈴虫、轡虫の声。また、鴉、ひばり、うずら。合わせた唇を平たく前の方へ突きだして、おけらの声。寝静まったらしい近所へは少し迷惑だろうがと言って、雄鶴雌鶴の啼き分け。また草ひばりの声もきかせた。

casual.en: To every cry, every cry, the listeners being listeners he could go all out, and they all seemed to be listening quietly, and it went as he wished and he was satisfied, and meaning for a bonus to show them the voice of the earthworm, "What they generally call an earthworm crying, that they say is the voice of the mole-cricket, but the earthworm cries too, eh," with that for a preface giving again a voice something like the mole-cricket, "If with this you do their voice you will see. For that study I once sat up all night in the wood at the Veterans' Home, but when footsteps sound, their voice breaks off for a while. I crouch there and wait a bit and then try it again, and if our voice is exactly like theirs, they answer straight off, and if it is wrong, there is no reply."
casual.ja: どの啼き声にも、啼き声にも、聴き手が聴き手だけにこちらが奮発できたので、皆も静かに耳を傾けた様子が見えて、自分の思いどおり自分も満足した、そしてお負けとして蚯蚓の声をしてみせるつもりで、

casual.en: "I see, eh — for all you see of me I wasn't a farmer from the first, no, nor any born artiste neither, though I daresay that goes for any of us, eh," he joked, and then he told of old days that held memories even for him. After one arm and one leg had gone useless he had talked it over with his wife and turned candy-seller. But just blowing the Chinese flute and hobbling along, hobbling along, not the snottiest-nosed brat would buy from him. The first day was clean zero and on the second day at last he sold ten sen's worth. He left that one silver coin with the child to please him with it, and child being child, he set it down on the bridge rail and went off to play, and in between another child took it. On the third day too he went out for trade because he went, but this was never going to do, he gave up hope, and stretched his legs out on the Yoshiwara embankment and sat there in a daze, thinking. "It was here I got a heaven-sent idea, and got in me the makings of the performer I would be one day, eh," and having got a small laugh from his hearers with that, he moved on to how he learned the cry of the frogs. "Before I knew it, any number of frogs were crying out in the paddies." As now, he showed how he had turned his eyes that way then, stuck his face a little sideways, and a good deal handier than when he had tried it that time, closing his hand as if round an egg and bringing his mouth to the hole at the top, he let out a little kuk kuk of a cry. "When I tried it myself, out of all those many frogs just six or seven turned round my way. I thought that strange and wondered a while, and then once more," he said, changing to a kak kak of a voice to show them, "when I tried it, this time all the frogs except those six or seven turned to face me, every one of them."
casual.ja: 「なるほど、な。――わたくしはこれでも初めから百姓、いや、ドン芸人じゃアございません。もっとも、どなたでもそうでしょうが」と洒落てから、自分にも思い出の多い昔を語った。自分は片手片足が利かなくなってから、女房とも相談して飴屋になった。が、ただ唐人笛を吹いてひょこりひょこり歩いてるのでは、どんな鼻垂れ小僧でも買ってくれようはずがなかった。最初の日はまるでゼロであったが、二日目にやッと十銭分だけ売れた。その銀貨一つを子供に喜ばせかたがた預けておいたら、子供のことだから、それを橋の欄干に置き棄てて遊んでる間に他の子供に取られてしまった。三日目にも商売に出たは出たものの、こんなことではとてもだめだと失望して、かの吉原土堤の上に足を投げだして、ぼんやり考えこんでいた。「ここでわたくしは天来の思想を得て、他日芸人になる素養ができましたのでげすが」と、ちょッと聴き手を笑わせてから、かわずの啼き声を覚えた話しに移った。「ふと、気がつきますと、田ン圃でかわずがたくさん啼いている」自分は今、目をその方に向けた時の様子をして、顔を少し横に突きだし、その時やってみたよりもずッと上手な具合いに、玉子なりに握った手のうえの方の穴へ自分の口を持って行き、ちょッとくッくッという啼き声をきかせ、「自分もやってみると、多くのかわずのうちから六七匹だけがこちらの方へ向きなおった。これは不思議だとしばらく考えておりましたが、今一遍」と言って、かッかッと言う声に改めてみせ、「やってみると、今度はその六七匹を除いたあとのかわずがすッかりこちらを向いた」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The truth was, he did not suppose it had gone quite so cleanly as all that, but there was no witness who had stood by and seen it at the time, so with an easy mind he made the story pretty. "And what I found was, the first way of crying was the females, and the one after was the males. And there were only six or seven males there, and all the rest were females."
casual.ja: じつはそうすッかりうまく行ったとは思われなかったのだが、その時そばに見ていた証人があるわけでもないから、安心して話を綺麗にしてしまった。「そして分りましたのですが、前の啼き方はめすで、あとのはおすです。そうしてそこにはおすが六七匹いただけで、あとは皆めすであったのです」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Interesting!"

casual.en: "…" He had had the Tenjin-sama's praise, and his own delight welled up still more. "This was my first notion, eh," and then when he went to where the children gathered and showed them the mimicry, the candy sold better than you would think. And from the next day the frog candy-man was waited for wherever he went.
casual.ja: 「……」自分は天神様のお賞めにあずかって、いっそう自分の興も湧いてでた。「これがわたくしの思いつきでして」、それから子供の集まってるところへ行ってその真似をしてみせると、案外によく飴が売れた。そしてその翌日からはかわずの飴屋がどこへ行っても待ち設けられた。

casual.en: "Sensei, candy is quite a paying thing, eh, with only five sen laid out it came to thirty sen, forty sen at the time."

casual.en: "What made you give up such a good paying line, then?"
casual.ja: 「そんなにいい儲け口を止めてしまったのには？」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Why, my hobby got too much for me, eh. Shall I say mimicking the cry of things was in me by nature? I mimic anything. No, whatever cries, if I cannot mimic it I study it till I can. Among my customers there are often orders like cry the firefly or cry the colic-worm, but that not even a genius beyond me could likely do. As for me, nowadays cats fighting and the cries of insects and birds have got common, and I cannot keep up unless I mimic aeroplanes and motorcars too."
casual.ja: 「そりゃア、わたくしの道楽が嵩じましたのです、な。わたくしには物の啼き声を真似るのが持ち前に備わってたとでも申すのでしょうか？　何でも真似ます。いや、すべて啼く物で真似ができなけりゃア、できるまで研究いたします。お客さまのうちにはよく螢を啼けとか、疝気の虫を啼けとかいう註文が出ますが、それはわたくし以上の天才にもおそらくできますまい。わたくしとしては、今じゃア、猫の喧嘩や虫、鳥の啼き声では平凡になって、飛行器や自動車の真似もしなけりゃア追ッつきません」

Rather than that, why not talk just as you told your own history now, natural and without frills, even when you go to the yose. Wouldn't that be a good deal more natural and interesting?" said the Tenjin-sama-like man again.

casual.label: house-checked

casual.ja: 「そりゃそうだ、ね」高見さんは両の膝を両手で抱いていながら、こちらの味方らしく言った。「この人の臨機応変の皮肉や冷かしと来たら、ずいぶん痛快ですよ」

casual.en: "In return, when I get to a certain point, I make my compromise and my concession, eh. There are times I even cry the firefly and the colic-worm for them. They are things that do not cry in any case, so it does not matter how I do it, see," and then putting on a sharp look, "You don't understand much yourself, eh, can a colic-worm cry? If that will not do for you, I've took your gate money already, so you can get off home quick — only that would be too bare, so at the end I let the other fellow save face too — but you don't want to go home halfway either, do you. Truth is, I don't want to send you home either — that is what I make of it."
casual.ja: 「その代り、こちらもまたあるところまで行くていと、妥協や譲歩をしておきます、な。螢や疝気の虫を啼いてみせることもございます。どうせ啼く物でないから、どういう風にでもかまわないわけでげすが」と、それからきッとした見えになり、「おめえさんもずいぶんわからねい、な、疝気の虫が啼けるかい？　それが不満足なら、どうせ、もう木戸銭は取ってあるのだから、とッとと帰ってもいいぞ――これだけではあまり殺風景になりますから、最後には向うにも花を持たせまして――だが、おめえさんだッても途中から帰りたくはなかろう。おいらもじつは帰したくねいんだ――てなことにしてしまいます」

casual.en: "That, I take it, is a kind of conclusion, eh." This was Nekohachi trying to take back what he felt he had fumbled a little earlier over the ending of the Tiger. "But then, when I get called to the princes and the like, why, gyagya-gya," and with that baring his teeth, goggling his eyes, screwing his face into something queer, he showed them cats at it fighting, and set them all off at once. But keeping a straight face himself, he went on, "It is not barnyard fowl, showing you cats kicking at each other is still hardly out of place. When the person before me is a lady, I can well hear the laugh from behind the fan where she hides her noble face. But at times, when I went up to Mr ___ for instance, I was told, they say you are good not only at mimicry but at rakugo too, let our guests hear something funny, so I declined. It is far too awesome for me, I cannot. But I was pressed, so perform a turn I did, perform one I did, and it is a strange thing, from the very start not a bit of it gets across. As we only know our own low-down society, of course the story falls there too. 'Oi, Hachi, are you there,' says I," and with that he showed hitching his backside and sitting on the step at the entrance, "from the first that does not get across what it is about, 'beranmei, bare-arsed you cannot hitch up, eh,' none of that ready wit gets across. Begging pardon for a rude thing to say, there is nothing to bite on, where there ought to come a roar they all sit prim."
casual.ja: 「やはり、一種の結論でしょう、な」これは猫八には先に虎のお終いでちょッと言い損ないをしたと思えた、その取り返しのつもりであった。「ところが、これが宮様がたなどへ招かれてまいりますていと、ぎゃぎゃぎゃアなんて」と、突然歯をむきだし、目を躍らせ、顔を珍妙にしがめて、猫の喧嘩する時の様子をしてみせ、皆を一度に吹きださしめた。が、自分はすまして、言葉を続けた、「庭鳥じゃアない、猫の蹴合いをお見せ申すにはまだ差し支えはございません。先様が御婦人である場合などには、やんごとなきお顔をお隠しになる扇の影からもそのお笑いがよく伺われます。が、時によりますと、――○○○様へあがった時などは、お前は物真似ばかりでなく、落語というものも巧みだそうだから、ひとつおもしろいのをお客さま方にお聴かせ申せと言われましたので、わたくしはお断りいたしました。とても畏れ多くてできません。けれども、たってと言われたので、一席願いましたことは願いましたが、――妙なもので、初手から少しもお分りになりません。どうせわたくしどもはわたくしどもの劣等な社会の事しか存じませんから、自然その話もそこへ落ちます。――おい、八公、いたか」と言って、尻を捲くって上り框へ腰かける様子をしてみせ、「これがそもそも何の事だか通じないのですから、――べらんめい裸じゃア尻は捲くれねいから、な、なんていう気を利かしたおもしろ味も通じません。失礼な申し分ではございますが、まったく張り合いがない、どッと来べきところをでも皆様がたはおすましになっておられます」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It's because the way you live is clean different, you know."
casual.ja: 「そりゃ生活がまるで違ってるから、ね」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That would be it, eh." He thought these learned gents were different after all. What he had run up against himself in the flesh and still could not explain, they had made clear for him in a single word. Truly the life of the upper folk and the life of the likes of us is clean different. The way we live is as far apart as the moon and a soft-shell turtle.
casual.ja: 「そうでげしょう、な」彼はさすがに学問ある人の仲間は違うものだと考えられた。こちらが自分で実際に当ってきながら、しかも自分では説明しきれなかったことをも、彼らのうちではたッた一言で分らせてくれた。本統に上つ方と自分らとの生活がまるで違ってるのだ。暮し方に月と鼈との相違がある。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Thinking so, he had the back row-houses in mind. First the blacksmith, slow to get going, always getting shouted at by his mountain-goddess. Next the woman hairdresser, no telling how many men she has gone through. Next to her our own place, and next to that the tram conductor, clattering about while folk are still sound asleep and off out to his bell-ringing trade. And right at the dead end the blear-eyed lame clam-seller. In summer they are a near stark-naked society, but of the lot only our place is anything like human. The field work is only my spare-time work, but even so there is an ease there those gaunt craze-driven lot know nothing of. And the daikon and leaf greens I give away free to them at times. For all that we are born-and-bred Edokko who keep no overnight money, I born from a geisha's belly in a famous Asakusa restaurant, my wife first-bathed in Kanda upper water. And with that he wanted to show off a bit of what he knew before them all.
casual.ja: こう思って、自分は自分らの裏長屋の事を心に浮べていた。とッつきが怠けがちの鍛冶屋で、いつもその山の神に怒鳴られてる。その次ぎが女髪結いで、男が何人代ったか分らない。その隣りが自分の家で、そのまた次ぎには電車の車掌がいて、人のまだよく眠ってる時からがたッぴしやりだして、ちんちん屋の商売に出て行きゃアがる。そしてどん詰りには、目ッかちで跛足の蜆屋がいる。夏は皆ほとんど真ッ裸かの社会であるが、そのうちでも人間らしいのはまず自分のところばかりだ。百姓はほんの自分の片手間仕事だが、それでもそこにあのがりがり妄者どもの知らぬ余裕がある。そして大根や菜ッ葉をも時々は彼らにただ分配してやってる。これでも自分らは宵越しの金は持たぬちゃきちゃきの江戸ッ子で、自分は芸者の腹から浅草の有名な料理屋に生れ、女房も神田上水に産湯を使ったものだ。ついでに自分の見識を皆の前に披露したくなった。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: There was a time a grand carriage stopped at the mouth of our row, you see. They must have known well enough how poor we lived, but, "Is this the house of the performer called Nekohachi?" "Yes," and I was a bit put to it by that. "Then is the master himself at home?" "Yes, the master has just gone to the bath and is out," hardly could I step out as the man himself in nothing but a loincloth, eh. "If you will wait a moment, I will go and call him directly," I said, and stepped outside for the moment. I gave my wife a wink, but she made an awkward face. I made as if to leave the house and slipped straight into the blacksmith's by the entrance, told his wife the story and got her to bring a kimono and sash, and putting on the look of a man just back from the bath, with a borrowed towel wetted with water and a soap box in hand, "Sorry to have kept you waiting, I am Nekohachi, what is your business?" Pupil and master with faces not a bit different, no wonder they found it strange. "In fact I have come from the ___ house, and just now your name came up there, and as you are said to do an amusing act you are to come at once, so I was told to come and fetch you," that is what he said.
casual.ja: 「ある時、わたくしの長屋の入り口に立派な馬車が停りました。どうせまずい生活をしているのは御承知であったでげしょうが、――猫八と申す芸人の家はこちらか？――へいと、わたくしはちょッと当惑いたしました。――では、本人は在宅かどうか？――へい、師匠は今湯にまいって留守ですが――まさか、ふんどし一つのわたくしがその本人ですとは出られませんから、な。――ちょッとお待ちを願います、ただ今すぐ呼んでまいりますから――と言ってひとまずそとへ出ました。女房にはちょッと目くばせいたしましたが、気まずい顔をしておりました。――わたくしは家を出るていと、すぐ入り口の鍛冶屋へはいり、そこのかみさんに訳を話して衣物と帯とを持ってきてもらいまして、今湯から帰ってきた風をして、借りた手拭いを水に濡らしたのと石鹸箱とを持って、――お待たせいたしました、すみません、わたくしが猫八ですが、御用は？――弟子と師匠とが少しも顔が違ってませんから、向うも不思議に思ったのは止むを得ません。――じつは、○○家から来たのだが、同家ではただ今お前の話が出て、おもしろい芸をする者だそうだからすぐ来るように言ってこいとのことだが、と言うのでした」

casual.en: Just then the near-sighted man said he would be in a fix if it got any later, and stood up. casual.en: He bore it, thinking it would be clear when this meeting broke up, which would be any moment now. But starting with Takami-san, no one considerately made a move, and to go dully home ahead of the rest would be dull too, so he took the host's wife again for company and talked of his own plot, what till now he had left forgotten. It was nothing he made trade of, particularly, but when talk turned to the plot, whoever he had for his listener, he at times grew so keen he forgot himself, and the spirit came back into him. This, as he had long thought, was his own taste, his pleasure. So,

casual.en: It was close on one in the morning, when the cranes crying over at the Veterans' Home came through clear, and everyone got to their feet. He got to his feet too, brisk on purpose, and went down the stairs with the rest, but with the old magazines and the leftover cakes and senbei stuffed in his breast, if that was to take the place of tonight's thanks, it felt silly, and here in secret he wanted to hold that tiger close and cry a while somehow. It was not that he was fretting because he had got no money, that much he knew from the point of being an Edokko — and that too you would know if you saw how his wife, an Edokko herself, gave in to a woman's weak heart and now and then tried to save up overnight money, and he knocked her about till she spent it all — but set beside a farmer's working life, this body of his that had to show people worthless tricks to live on felt sad somehow, all over again.
casual.ja: 廃兵院で鶴の啼く声が澄みわたってよく聞える午前の一時近くになって、皆が席を立った。自分もわざと潔く立って、皆といっしょに二階を下りたが、ふところへねじこんだ古雑誌と菓子や煎餅の残物とが今夜のお礼代りかと思えば、ばかばかしいような気もして、ここでひそかに例の虎と抱き合ってしばらく何だか泣いてみたかった。けっして金の貰えないのをくよくよ思ってるわけでないのは、自分が江戸ッ子たる点に照り合わせても分ってるが、――そしてこれも江戸ッ子たる女房が、女の弱い気に負けて、時々よい越しの金を残そうとするのを、自分が投ぐりつけてまで使わせてしまうところを見てもらっても、分ってるが、――百姓の労働生活に比べてみると、自分は人にくだらない芸などを見せてそれで生活をしなければならぬ身が、今さらに何となく悲しかった。

But for himself — perhaps out of a nasty habit — what a stingy spirit, he thought himself mean. And if he could have it, he wanted to quit being a performer from tomorrow.

Then what looked like harmless words came rattling out. "Had your one already? This slump and all, Sensei looks to be doing pretty well for himself — let me have a bit of it, what do you say? curious.en: "ha, ha, ha!" The man holding his seat across the way and staring this way laughed again.
curious.ja: 「は、は、はア！」筋向うに座を占めてこちらを見詰めていた男がまた笑った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: So long as he heard people laughing it rang pleasant in him, and yet it was strange that there was nothing funny to himself at all. If you wanted the comedian's logic for it, there was plenty and to spare. That to make people laugh there is no effect in laughing yourself is one of them. And yet, though he held off even from the drink people like, to protect this voice he uses for the trade, when he faced people he still had to make it look as if he drank. Could there be such hardship in any other work. People think a comedian just breezes along with no troubles in the world, but let them try being the man himself. He is thick with troubles people know nothing of. A man like himself is as if made out of a lump of trouble.
curious.ja: 人の笑いさえ聞えれば、自分には気持ちよく響くのであるが、自分自身には少しもおもしろくないのが不思議であった。芸人としての理窟を言えば、それはたくさんあることはある。人を笑わせるには自分から笑っていては利き目がないということもその一つだ。けれども、自分は人の好む酒をもさし控えて、この商売に使う自分の声を保護しているくせに、人に向ってはやッぱり酒を呑むかのごとく見せかけなければならぬ。こんな苦しいことが他の仕事にもあろうか？　人は芸人なんてしゃアしゃアして、世に苦労もないように思ってるが、その本人にもなってみるがいい。人の知らない苦労をこてこてとしている。自分なんかはまるで苦労の固まりでもってできたような人間である。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Still, for one pleasure, he had pulled out the back fence of his row-house lodgings, and from there rented cheap from long back the open ground that lay beyond, and grew vegetables there. And when they came up plenty, not only did his own family eat them, he shared them out to the neighbours round about as well. Just to see the neighbours pleased was another pleasure in itself.
curious.ja: それでも、一つ楽みなことには、自分の長屋住いのうら垣根をぶん抜いて、そこから出たところの明き地を前々から安く借りて、野菜を作っている。そして多くできた時は、自分の家族がそれを喰うばかりでなく、隣り近所のものにも分配してやる。近所のものが喜ぶのを見るだけでもまた一つの楽みである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The green caterpillars and black worms that get on the leaves of little turnips and daikon, you dig a ditch along the ridges, and shake the leaves toward it, and they all come rolling down. Then you stamp them all at once, or the children prod them with the end of a stick, and kill them.
curious.ja: 小かぶや大根の葉につく青虫や黒虫は、畝並みに溝を掘っておいて、そこへ向って葉を振うと、皆ころころと落ちてしまう。それを一どきに踏みつけたり、子供なぞ棒の先で突ッついたりして、殺すのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Of late he had set out cucumber and eggplant seedlings as well, so the cutworms had to be watched. Like thieves, like us, the things do their work only by night, so hunt for them by day and you never see a sign of them. Tonight, he was thinking, the moment supper was done he would strip to his loincloth and have a child hold the lantern for him out in the field, and make a thorough job of doing for the cutworms.
curious.ja: 昨今は胡瓜や茄子の苗をも植えつけたので、根切り虫に注意してやらねばならぬ。この虫は泥棒や自分たちと同様、夜業ばかりする奴だから、昼間探しても少しだッて姿を見せぬ。今夜はひとつ、晩飯をすませるとすぐ、自分はふんどし一つになり、子供に提灯を持たせて畑に行き、十分に根切り虫の退治をやってやろうと考えられた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then the little-Buddha Sensei opened his eyes wide. "No more work tonight, I suppose?"
curious.ja: すると、この時、小大仏の先生が目を見ひらいて、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「今夜は、もう、用がなかろう」と尋ねた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Yes, I have got my two kōza behind me, but —" That did not feel like answer enough, so catching what the other was driving at, "Might I tag along with you somewhere tasty, eh?"
curious.ja: 「へい、高座は二個所すましてまいりましたが――」これでは自分の返事が足りないようにも思えたので、彼は向うの意味を汲み取って、「どこかうまいところへお伴できますか、な？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Oh, if it is only home to bed for you, why not come along with me?"
curious.ja: 「なアに、どうせうちへ帰って寝るだけのことなら、どうだ、おれについてこないか？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I will come — on your orders, anywhere." Even to Kegon Falls, the song says — the words came unbidden to his lips.
curious.ja: 「まいりましょう――あなたのお指図なら、どこへでも」どこ、華厳の滝までもという歌を――思わず――口もとまで思い浮べた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It is a study group of writers, you know, no harm in listening a while. Come now and it is only two hours to stick out. Afterwards I will make it your world."
curious.ja: 「ある文士たちの研究会だが、ね、聞いていてためにならないことでもない。これから行けば、もう、たッた二時間の辛抱だ。そのあとはお前の世界にしてやるから」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That sounds fun, eh, I'll come along too, to learn a thing or two, eh." He answered light enough, but he was fretting whether the load he had just set down would be loaded on his back again tonight. For him there was no time when body and mind felt lighter than in the tram on the way home after doing his union turn each night. From what he had heard he could not get home for at least another two or three hours. And in that time those cutworms might have cut through the roots of two or three of the seedlings in his plot, for all he knew.
curious.ja: 「そりゃアおもしろいでしょう、な、わたくしも後学のためにお伴いたしましょう」そうは軽い気持ちで答えたけれども、今しがたやッと下してきた重荷を今夜また今一度背負わされはしないかということを案じられた。自分には、毎晩組合の義務を果して帰るさの電車の中ほど軽い身心になってる時はほかにないのである。聴いたところでは、今からなお少くとも二三時間は家に帰れない。してみると、その間にも畑の植えつけ苗の根を二本でも三本でもあの根切り虫に切られているかも分らないのだ。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: With that worry on one side of his mind, the tram soon reached the terminus, so he stuffed the Kōdan Club inside his coat and got up after Takami-san, carrying his crippled body hobble hobble toward the exit. For a dozen years and more now his rheumatism had left him all but palsied down one side. Crippled as no one else is, he was thankful, as the saying goes that art saves the man, that he could still keep wife and children fed like anyone else.
curious.ja: 一方にそれを気にしながらも、やがて電車が終点に着いたので、彼も講談倶楽部を懐中にねじこんで、高見さんの後から立ちあがり、ひょこりひょこりと、不自由なからだを出口の方へ運んだ。彼はこの十数年来リョウマチのために半身不随のようになってるのである。人並みならぬこんな身体をしていても、芸が身を助けるの諺で、妻子をまず人並に養って行けるのがありがたかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Walking along in silence he was apt to sink into earnest thoughts like these, when a fat woman he knew met him and broke them up again.
curious.ja: 黙って歩いてると、こんなきまじめな考えに沈みがちであるのを、ふと、知り合のでぶでぶ女に出会ってまたうち破られた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Nekohachi-san!" Pushing her fat bulk on ahead of her as if proud of it, she called out to him as they passed, though she need not have, in a gentle voice that did not match the bulk, "Home now?"
curious.ja: 「猫八さん！」かの女はその太った図体を自慢そうに前の方へ運ばせながら、行き違いに、止せばいいのに、こちらへ、その図体にも似合わぬ優しい声をかけた、「今、お帰り？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Well, General Oyama!" He just had to tease again, so he teased as he always did. He turned sideways toward her and pulled himself up stiff and solemn to a stop, but she went off laughing, so he let her go out of his sight and chased her with words alone, "I've one more party to do yet, eh."
curious.ja: 「いよう、大山大将！」彼はついまた冷かしてみたくなって、いつもどおり冷かした。横にその方へ向いてぎょうぎょうしく立ち停ったのだが、女が笑いながら行ってしまうので、自分の目を放して言葉でだけ追いかけさせた、「今一つお座敷があるので、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's it," came the answer from behind. "You really are an earner!"
curious.ja: 「そう」という返事は後ろに聴えていた。「ほんとにあなたは稼ぎ手よ！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Why, whether it would turn into money or not he didn't know, but with her carrying that body along as if to boast of it, he just wanted to boast of something himself, so he had called the place he was off to now a party.
curious.ja: 「………」なアに、金になるのかどうかは分らないのであるが、向うがいかにも自慢げに見えるようにあのからだを運んでるので、こちらもただ何か自慢してやりたくなって、今からさして行く所をお座敷と言ってみたのだ。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "A stout-built woman, eh," Takami-san said.
curious.ja: 「でッぷりした女だ、な」と、高見さんは言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "How so — for all that, her husband dotes on her, so there's no standing against her, you know!"
curious.ja: 「どうして――あれでなかなか亭主にゃア可愛がられておりますからたまりませんや！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Takami-san was listening in earnest, but he himself knew nothing of the sort in fact. So long as it was a joke that was all he wanted. Thinking this man too was no great talker after all, he changed the subject.
curious.ja: 高見さんはまじめに聴いていたが、自分にはじつはそんなことは分ってないのであった。ただ冗談でありさえしたらよかったのだ。この人も案外話せないと思いながら、話題を転じた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It's quite hot, isn't it, eh? At this rate will this rainy season be a dry rainy season, eh? That's trouble, eh."
curious.ja: 「なかなか暑いじゃアございませんか？　この分じゃア、この梅雨は乾梅雨でげしょうか、な？　困ります、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Why, if it rains the feet coming to the yose will thin out, eh."
curious.ja: 「そりゃア、雨が降れば寄席の客あしも減じようから、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "As for customers' feet, I'm seasoned to rubbing little sticks, you know. I've borrowed a bit of another man's ground and I'm growing vegetables. The trouble is that, if the rain doesn't come when it should, they won't do right, eh."
curious.ja: 「お客の足なら、摺り小木にもなれでさア。わたくしはちッとばかり人の地面を借りて野菜を作っております。困るのアそれが、雨が降るべき時に降らないとうまく行きませんから、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 二
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Talking this over as they went, they turned in at the gate of a house. That even here a little patch of cucumbers had been made struck him as genteel.
curious.ja: こんなことを語ってるうちに、ある家の門をはいった。ここにもわずかばかりだが胡瓜の畑を作ってあるのが彼には奥床しかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: To get up to the second floor of that house he could only twist his backside up in a queer bobbing way. But when Takami introduced him to the party of six or seven with, "I've brought a rare guest along tonight. I thought we might have him do something for us later. This is the Nekohachi you've heard of," he felt the same pride as always when he cozies up to his customers.
curious.ja: その家の二階へ上るにも、彼は変てこに尻をひょこひょこ曲げてでなければ上れなかった。けれども、自分の事を、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「今夜は珍らしいお客さんを一人連れてきた」と言って、高見さんが六七名の一座へ紹介してくれた時には、自分もいつもどおりお客に嬌えこんだ時のような誇りを感じた。「あとでひとつやってもらってもいいと思って――例の猫八です」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "This should be fun," somebody cried out.
curious.ja: 「こりゃアおもしろかろう」と叫ぶものもあった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That 'the' I took to, eh, I'm a performer with a bit of a name myself, you know. So to come out before great literary gentlemen like yourselves, eh, and not feel stage fright like that, that's lucky for me." Saying this he glanced round the party. Some laughed innocently and none seemed to have taken offence, so he took them for people who would generously take his joke. But to make surer still, meaning to make them understand more, "Only let me tell you beforehand, with rheumatism my body doesn't work like other people's. So if I look to be sitting up stiff like this on purpose, that's why it is, eh, it's not exactly that I'm trembling before you gentlemen."
curious.ja: 「例のは気に入りました、な、わたくしも多少は知られた芸人ですから。あなたがたのような偉い文士方の前へ出ましても、な、その、そうおじ気が出ないのは仕合せです」こう言ってじろりと一座を見わたすと、無邪気に笑ったものもあるし、別に感触を害しているようなものもないらしいので、こちらの洒落を皆寛大に理解してくれる人々だと分った。が、なお念のためにもッと分らせておくつもりで、「ただし前もってお断わりしておきますが、わたくしはリョウマチのために人様のようにはからだが利きません。したがって、こうわざと畏まってますように見えるのもそのためでげして、あながち諸君を怖がってるわけではございません」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "ha, ha, ha" came, so he felt safe for a start, and thinking they were his now he shut his mouth for a while.
curious.ja: 「は、は、は」と来たので、彼はまず安心して、もう、こちらの物だとしばらく口をつぐんでしまった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: A study of somebody's novel had begun, but as the subject was actors, he pricked up his ears as a performer in something of the same line.
curious.ja: 誰かの書いた小説の研究が初まってるのであったが、題目は俳優の事であるから、彼も縁の近い芸人として聞き耳を立てた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The man who looked to be the master of the house was someone he had often bathed with in the bathhouse two or three years ago and still met on the road now and then, and he said to Takami-san, "We are just now on 'Tiger.'"
curious.ja: 当家の主人らしいのは、二三年前にはよく銭湯でいっしょになり、近ごろでも時々途中で出会うことがある人だが、これが高見さんに向って、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「今、『虎』が問題になってるところです」と言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Whose?"
curious.ja: 「誰れのです？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "'Tiger' by Kume. It came out in the May Bunsho Sekai."
curious.ja: 「久米氏の虎です、五月の文章世界に出た」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I haven't read it," Takami-san answered.
curious.ja: 「僕は読んでませんが」と、高見さんは答えた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Few here have read it either — and as the man who went out of his way to put it forward for the June meeting isn't here tonight, I was thinking of letting it pass without a word."
curious.ja: 「ここにも読んでる人は少いのだが――これをわざわざ六月の会に持ちだしておいたその人が今夜出席していないので、何も言わないで通過してしまおうかと思ってるのです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: To the question, "What sort of story is it?" the host answered, "I only glanced through it because he asked me by postcard to bring it up — thin if you call it thin, but neatly put together at its low level. The author can hardly have demanded much of himself, so for that author it will do well enough, I suppose — 'Tiger' is the part the hero, a comic actor, has been cast to play. To quote the original, this actor 'had a child already eight years old. And the child had trodden his first stage last year and had before him a future as a shinpa actor like him, no, more proper than him. He thought he would never make the child a comic.'"
curious.ja: 「どんな筋なんでしょう」という問いに主人は答えて、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「僕もその人が問題にしてくれろと、ハガキで言ってきてあったのでちょッと読んでおいただけなのですが、――浅薄と言えば浅薄な物だが、低い程度で器用には纒まってると思う。作者にもそう深い要求がなかったのだろうから、あの作者としてはあれでもいいのでしょうが――虎とは作の主人公なる三枚目俳優が扮することになった役目です。この俳優には、原文を引くと、『もう、八歳になる子があった。そしてその子は去年初舞台を踏んで彼と同じく否、彼よりももッと正式な、新派俳優になる未来をもっていた。彼はその子をけっして三枚目にはしたくないと思った』」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Hearing this reading, Nekohachi felt he had walked into an awful place. He knew himself that this was a bit of an overblown thought, and yet it sounded just as if they were talking about himself. He had four boys, the eldest fourteen in first year of higher primary, the next twelve in fifth year of elementary, both doing well and both monitors. This twelve year old was good at mimicking his father, and had an art even beyond his father's, but for all that he would not make him a second Nekohachi. No, it was just so as not to let the children see their father mimicking cat fights and animal voices and coaxing good humour out of the customers from up on the koza that he had long ago gone out of his way to choose this inconvenient suburb to live in. Cat turned to tiger, there was no great difference in that.
curious.ja: 「………」この本読みを聴いて猫八はえらいところへ飛びこんできたものだと思われた。この思いは自分でも少しおおげさな考えだとは承知しながら、まるで自分の事を言われているようであった。自分には男の子が四人あって、総領は十四で高等一年、次ぎは十二で尋常五年、いずれも出来がよくて級長をしている。この十二のが父親の真似が上手で、しかも父親以上の芸を持ってるが、それでも第二の猫八にはしたくないのである。否、父親が猫の喧嘩や動物の声を真似して、高座のうえから客の機嫌を取ってるところを子供に見せたくないためにこそ、早くからわざわざこんな不便な郊外を選んで住んでるのだ。猫が虎に変っても、そこにたいした相違はない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "The part handed him was just the one part of the tiger." What the host was reading seemed to be the text of the story itself. "Not a man's name. Just the one part dressed up as a real beast of a tiger. He had even taken the byname of animal actor, so what wonder now to be handed the tiger to play. And yet he felt a little sad. Used to it as he long was, profession as he thought it, teasing as he knew it to be, he felt the human inside him being made a fool of, and even felt a little angry. The hero is in that sort of *situation*."
curious.ja: 「彼の振られた役というのは、ただ虎の一役だッた」主人が読んでるのはその小説の本文らしかった。「人の名ではない。ほんとのけだ物の虎に扮する一役だけだッた。動物役者という異名をさえ取っていたので、今さら虎の役を振られたとて、それが何の不思議であろう。けれども、ちょッと悲しく感じた。長年馴れてきていながら、職業だと思っていながら、どうせ茶化しているのだとは思いながら、自分の中なる人間がばかにされてるような気がして、ちょッと腹立たしくさえ思ったというようなシチュエイションにある主人公です」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Quite deftly the point the author was aiming at holds together throughout," put in the man with the face like Tenjin-sama, in an earnest tone.
curious.ja: 「なかなか器用には作者の狙ったところは一貫しています」と、天神さまみたような顔つきの人が熱心な口調で口を出した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" The English word situation the host had just used stayed in Nekohachi's ears, and he took it to mean something like a painful fix you get caught in. And he himself was in fact fitted into his customers' favour, and had gone and fitted himself right into it, till he was in the state he was in now where he could move neither one way nor the other, so he joked it to himself, quiet. But down underneath he felt the hateful part of the performer's trade all the more.
curious.ja: 「………」猫八には、今主人が言ったシチュエイションという英語が耳に残って、苦しいはめといったような意味の言葉ではないかしらんと想像された。そして自分は実際にお客様方の御贔負についはめられて、それに自分もついはまりこみ、とうとう二進も三進も動けない今の身分になってるのだとひそかに洒落れてみた。が、その心の奥ではますます芸人のいやなことを感じた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "There is the place where the leader points it out, eh, says that is just Fukai-kun's fitted part," said the priest-like one, close-cropped, with bumps rising fore and aft like a mountain range, the knowing face.
curious.ja: 「座長がそりゃア深井君のはまり役だと指摘するところがあります、ね」と、五分刈りあたまの前後へむッくり山脈のできた善智識顔の坊さんらしいのが言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "And then they tell him the whole act will be eaten clean up by Fukai-kun's tiger, and such," the host went on, "and he got that much proud again even. But being the tiger, with no lines to say, there was no call to turn up for rehearsals even. Glad to make use of the day when the child begged to go to Ueno Zoo, he says, well then shall I show you the much talked of hippo, while in truth he means to go and study how a tiger looks. Then on the way, in the tram, he meets a theatre critic, and is asked where he is off to, so he answers, truth to tell, to the zoo to show the child the much talked of hippo, but the sharp critic has him marked, that is a lie, I have heard it already, it is the tiger really."
curious.ja: 「それから他のものにもその幕はすッかり深井君の虎に喰われてしまうというようなことを言われて」と、主人は言葉を進めた、「彼はいくらかまた得意にさえなった。けれども、虎だから、台辞を言うことがないので稽古にも出る必要がない。その日を利用して子供は上野の動物園へ行ってくれろと言うのを幸い、じゃア近ごろ評判の河馬でも見せてやろうかと言って、その実、自分は虎の様子をでも研究してくるつもりになった。すると、途中、電車のうちである劇評家に出会い、どこへ行くのだと尋ねられたので、じつは、子供に大評判の河馬を見せに動物園までと答えたが、機敏な劇評家からそりゃア嘘だろう、もう聴いてるよ、じつは虎だろうと目星をさされた」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "There is a kind of sorrow comes out in a bit like that too," said the Tenjin-sama man.
curious.ja: 「そういうところにも一種の悲哀は出ています」と、天神さまが言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Nekohachi opened his eyes wide as if for the first time on hearing the word sorrow. It seemed to him more and more as if his own affair had been taken and remade and dug into. With his right hand stuck on the tatami and his left laid on the folded hand towel on his knee, admiring at how human feeling falls to the same place whoever feels it, he leaned his head a little back where he sat sideways and said, "I see! To an unlearned one like me a novel seemed a slapdash made-up thing with eight hundred lies strung together in it — though that may have been rude from the start to Sensei gentlemen like yourselves — but to hear it now, sure enough it aims at the true thing, it does, eh"
curious.ja: 「………」猫八は悲哀という言葉を聴いて、今さらのように目を見張った。ますます自分のことでも作り換えて、うがってあるように思えたからである。右の手を畳に突いて、左りの手を膝の上にある畳んだ手拭いの上に置いてたのだが、人情というものは誰れが感じても結局こう同じところに落ちるのかと感心して、その横坐わりのままあたまを少し後ろへ反らせて「なるほど！　わたくしのような無学のものには小説なんかはいい加減に作り事を書いて、うそ八百を並べてあるものと思っておりましたが、――もっともこれはお歴々の先生方には初めから失礼であったかもしれませんが――今伺ってみますと、なるほど本統のことを狙ってあるものでげす、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Present-day novels are all like that, of course," the Tenjin-sama man answered, sounding a little angry. "We are different novelists from novelists who write lies and rest satisfied with it!"
curious.ja: 「今の小説はむろん皆そうだよ」例のは少し怒ったように答えた。「うそを書いて満足している小説家とは吾々は小説家が違います！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Fu, fun," went the knowledge-face man, laughing through his nose.
curious.ja: 「ふ、ふん」と鼻で笑うのは智識がおであった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "How you do flare up," said the very near-sighted-looking man, smiling as he teased him.
curious.ja: 「なかなか憤慨するじゃアありませんか」と、ひどい近眼らしい人もにッこりして冷かしを言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I am not flaring up in particular, only there are plenty of fools in the world who take slapdash popular novels like Hekirurien's or Tokutomi Roka's for the fine standard and pass low, vulgar criticism."
curious.ja: 「別に憤慨しているのではないけれど、世間にはよくばか者があって、碧瑠璃園や徳富蘆花のようないい加減な通俗小説をえい方の標準にして俗悪な批評をするものが多いから」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Terribly sorry, I am sure," Nekohachi said, keeping a straight face and dipping his head a little, and they all laughed. But this time that alone left him feeling unsatisfied, so he offered up one joke. "I for my part have never yet met a theatre critic in the course of my own researches, no, but once, to study the cry of the earthworm, I squatted up all night in the woods by the Veterans' Home over there, and they took me for a thief and a detective challenged me, he did, eh."
curious.ja: 「どうもすみません」猫八はすました顔でちょッと頭を下げたので、皆が笑った。が、それだけでは今度は自分が満足できないような気になって、一つ冗談を言った。「わたくしは、しかし研究の途中でまだ劇評家にはお会いしたことがございませんが、ある時、蚯蚓の啼き声を研究するために、あの、そこの廃兵院の森に夜明しをしてしゃがんでおりましたら、泥棒と見誤られて刑事に誰何されたことがございます」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That too, you know, is the result of a kind of sorrow or earnestness," was all the explanation Tenjin-sama gave, and from no one else came any ha, ha, ha.
curious.ja: 「それも、君、一種の悲哀かまじめかの結果だよ」という天神様の説明があっただけで、別に誰からも、は、は、はッとは来なかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Nekohachi felt the wind taken clean out of him, against all expectation. And for the first time it struck him that these were not his customers. As an entertainer he might make people cry or laugh, but he had no room left to cry or laugh himself. These people, though, were a cut above even that, for they seemed to study even the feeling of an entertainer himself who makes people cry or laugh and cannot cry or laugh himself. They were specialists in that line, right enough. At this rate an honest humility rose in him to take off his helmet cleanly and own himself beaten, and he asked, "And what did the actor do after that?" What he wanted to know most was about the child. All the same he had quite made up his mind the fall would be that he pleaded the part unworthy and did not go on the stage, or that at least he did not let the child come to the theatre.
curious.ja: 「………」猫八は予期に反して、がッくり調子抜けがした。そして初めて思い及んだのであるが、これは自分のお客ではない。自分は芸人として人を泣かせたり笑わせたりしても、自分の泣いたり笑ったりする余地を持たない。ところが、この人々はまた自分らよりも一段うわ手で、人を泣かせたり笑わせたりする芸人その物の自分では泣いたり笑ったりできないその心持ちまでも研究しているらしい。さすがはその方の専門家たちだろう。これじゃア自分は潔く兜を脱ごうという正直な謙遜心を起して、「そうしてその俳優はそれからどういたしました」と尋ねてみた。おもに子供との関係を知りたかったのである。それでも、たぶん、役不足を言って舞台に出なかったとか、子供だけは芝居へ見に来させなかったとかいうのが落ちだろうとたかをくくっていた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 三
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Just look. You've made a clean confession, haven't you, but if you want to see a tiger you needn't go all the way to the zoo — give anyone a litre or two and he'll turn into one, eh? — Why, shall we go and see that tiger over there? — That won't do. I can't shake this little one off, you see, and he looked back at the child again. There's a passage like that too," the host went on, still with an eye on the book. And everyone forgot Nekohachi and the rest and bent their hearts toward the tiger, but to Nekohachi that tiger was like himself. "For foolishness, Yui's part is much the same. Rather your single tiger part may be the honour, with the popularity gathering on the tiger alone, you know — thinking so I mean to do all I can with all my might, you know — Yes indeed, we for our part are rather counting on your tiger — Much obliged, and Fukai smiled wryly and yet was not a little comforted in his heart."
curious.ja: 「そうれ見たまえ。みごとに白状に及んだじゃないかね、しかし虎を見たいんならわざわざ動物園まで行くにも及ぶまいぜ。――一二升飲ませれゃ誰だってなりますが？――どうだい、そッちの虎を見に行こうじゃないか？――そいつアいけません。何しろこいつを撒くわけには行きませんからね、と彼はまた子供をかえりみた。というところもあるのだが」と、主人はなお本を見い見い語って行った。そして皆が猫八などのいるのを忘れて虎の方へ心を傾けたが、猫八にはその虎が自分のようであった。「ばかさ加減を言えば由井の役だッて同じようなものさ。むしろ君の虎一役が名誉かもしれんぜ、人気が虎の一身に集まったりして、ね。――そう思ってわたくしも一生懸命やるだけはやるつもりなんですが、ね。――そうとも、僕たちだッてむしろ君の虎に期待しているよ。――恐れ入ります、と深井は苦笑をしながらも、内心少からず慰められた」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That won't do, eh," Nekohachi said, screwing up his face, "to do that situation in a place like that!"
curious.ja: 「いけません、な」と、猫八は顔を顰めてみせながら、「そんなところで例のシチュエイションをやっては！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "ufu, fu," a stylish little laugh was heard.
curious.ja: 「うふ、ふ」と、乙な笑いが聞えた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Before gentlemen like you, for the likes of me to use cheeky English may have been a mistake —" He had thought better of it that this English might come to what they call compromise, but, "anyhow, if that actor they call Fukai lets the critic's puffing talk the decent human thought he had managed to hold in that case clean away, and goes carelessly getting into the swing again, that will be trouble, eh."
curious.ja: 「先生がたの前で、わたくし風情が、生意気な英語の使い方をしたのは間違ってるか存じませんが――」この英語はいわゆる妥協ということに当るのではないかと思いなおしたのだが、「とにかく、その深井とかいう俳優がその場合にせっかく持った真人間らしい考えを、劇評家の煽てでなくさせてしまい、うかうかとまた調子づいて行っちゃア困ります、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But that is just what makes it interesting, in a way —" the host said.
curious.ja: 「ところが、そうであるからかえっておもしろくもあるのだが――」と、主人は言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But as for me, a thing like that —" he said, turning earnest as if to show he was not fool enough for that, but neither the host nor any of the rest lent him an ear.
curious.ja: 「しかしわたくしならそんなことは」と、彼は自分をそんなばかでもないと弁護するように熱心じみたが、主人ばかりでなく皆も耳をかたむけてくれなかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "He went to the zoo and did no more than watch the tiger sitting still and yawning, and yet he came home thinking he had got the tiger's feelings better, somehow, than a handsome lover's feelings. When the first day came and the sewn-up tiger came onto the stage and yawned, at that alone there were cries of Fukai, Fukai! from the gallery, and he grew not a little proud. And at the fall of the curtain, when he leapt upon the heroine of the play, gallery first and the whole house with it gave him a great burst of applause."
curious.ja: 「動物園に行って虎のじッとしているところや欠伸をしたのを見ただけでも、彼はとにかく色男の気持ちよりも虎の気持ちをよく分ったと思って帰宅した。いよいよ初日が来て、縫いぐるみの虎が舞台に出て欠伸をすると、それだけでも大向うから深井、深井！　と呼ぶ声がかかったので、すくなからず得意になった。そしてその幕切れのところで劇の女主人公に躍りかかると、大向うを初めとして諸見物の大喝采を得た」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Isn't that making fools of people?" It was the words of the much younger man, speaking for the first time.
curious.ja: 「人をばかにしているじゃアありませんか？」これは初めて口に出すずッと若い人の言葉であった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That is making a fool of people, right enough," Tenjin-sama put in too, laughing this time.
curious.ja: 「そりゃ人をばかにしたもの、さ」と、天神さまも今度は笑いながら口出しをした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: A grudge rose in Nekohachi too about the way customers treat him on the kōza, enough to make him want to have his say. "From where I stand, it is the spectators he is making fools of, for getting delighted over trifles, and I daresay he is feeling for the actor himself, eh — spectators are the same as yose customers, you know."
curious.ja: 「………」猫八もまた何か言ってみたくなったほど高座で受けるお客からの待遇に対する不平が浮んでいた。「そりゃア、わたくしから見ますと、つまらないことを嬉しがる見物人の事をばかにしているのでごぜいまして、たぶんその俳優の本人には同情していてくれてるのでげしょう、な――見物なんて、寄席のお客も同様でげすから」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Now, about that," Takami-san put in his first question with a mild look, "is it a work where the author is being ironical — I have not read a scrap of it, so I can hardly have an opinion — but to go by what I have just heard?"
curious.ja: 「いったい、それは」と、高見さんは穏かな顔つきで初めて質問を出した、「作者が皮肉を言ってる作でしょうか――僕はさッぱり読んでいませんから、意見のあろうはずはないのですが、――今、聴いたところをもってみれば？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It is irony, to be sure," the knowledge-face man answered in a set-piece tone, "the question is whether the author can be satisfied with irony of so shallow a degree."
curious.ja: 「皮肉には違いないのですが」と、知識がおが切り口上で答えた、「こんな浅薄な程度の皮肉でも作者が満足できるかどうかが問題でしょう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That is it, I suppose." The near-sighted man spoke, for a near-sighted man, with unexpected crispness. "I have not read this one either, but what that lot write is all neatly put together in a small clever way, and without a scrap of *back* or depth."
curious.ja: 「そこだろう、ね」近眼は近眼らしくもなく案外にはきはきした言葉であった。「僕もこれは読んでいないが、いったい、あアいう連中の書いてる物はいずれも小器用には纒まってるが、少しも背景や深みがない」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Just as Nekohachi-kun said," the knowledge-face man went on, "the author's sympathy for the hero is to be seen, but the way that sympathy is shown is exceedingly thin."
curious.ja: 「今、猫八君も言われたとおり」と、知識がおは続けた、「主人公に対する作者の同情は見えてるが、その同情の現わし方がきわめて薄ッぺらなのです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Thin or not, it is not that it has no background of life." That was the host. "Only, one may say he is an author who can give it no more than a thin background. As for T-kun going out of his way to propose this work, as he is not here tonight his true intent is unclear, but I take it he wanted to make a question for debate of the way it is both put together and yet somehow wanting."
curious.ja: 「薄ッぺらでも生活背景がないことはない」これは主人の発言であった。「ただ薄ッぺらな背景しか持たせることのできない作者だと言えば言えるのだ。Ｔ君がこの作をわざわざ提議したのも、今夜出席していないからその真意は分らないけれども、たぶん、纒まってもいるし、またどこか物足りないしというようなところを疑問にして評議してみたかったのだろうと思われる」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I daresay that is it."
curious.ja: 「そりゃたぶんそうだろう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Nekohachi wanted to make them all laugh by saying he did not know what the hell a *back* or a *haikei* was, but as what he had said had been taken up as a point he held his nose high and, with a solemn-looking face, "And so, is this novel finished with that, eh — is there no other fall to it?"
curious.ja: 「………」猫八にはバックとかハイケイとかが何のヘラだか分りませんと言って、皆を笑わしてみたかったが、自分の言ったことを問題に採用してもらったので鼻を高くして、まじめくさった顔で、「そうして、この小説はそれでお終いでげしょうか――何か別に落ちでも？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: ha, ha, ha! Only two or three of them just laughed.
curious.ja: 「は、は、はア！」二三名がただ笑うだけであった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: To Nekohachi it felt like the roar had come at a strange place.
curious.ja: 「………」猫八には変なところでどッと来たものだと思われた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "You're no rakugo man," Tenjin-sama had stuck in another unasked word, or so it felt to Nekohachi, but he saw at once his own ignorance was being teased, so he buried his awkwardness in another apology.
curious.ja: 「落語家じゃないよ」と、天神さまがまた入らざる口を出したと思われたが、猫八はすぐ自分の無学を冷かされたのだと分ったので、極りが悪いのをまた謝罪にまぎらせてしまった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Yes, quite sorry about that."
curious.ja: 「へい、どうもすみません」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "There is no ochi, no fall, in a novel, but what Nekohachi would take for a fall is what closes this story, and it is that which keeps the piece, thin as it is, alive. Fukai gets his great applause at the curtain and is going off proud in his sewn-up shape when from the shadow of the dark flats someone cries 'Father' and flings himself upon him.
