He looks back in surprise and finds his own child crying, child as he is, at the foolish part his father has played. He too cannot help crying, now at last. And then, 'the tiger and the human child wept together for a while in the shadow of the dark background,' that is how it ends."
curious.ja: 「小説には落ちなんかはないが」と、主人は言葉を改めた、「猫八なら落ちともみるだろうと思われることがこの小説を結んでいて、しかもそれがためにこの一篇を浅薄ながら生かしているのだ。深井は幕切れに大喝采を得て縫いぐるみの姿で得意そうに引上げる時、暗い書き割りのかげから『お父さん』と言って自分に飛びついたものがある。びッくりして見返ると、自分の子供が父のあまりばかばかしい役をしたのを子供ながら泣いているのであった。自分も今さらのごとく泣かざるを得なかった。そして『虎と人間の子とは暗い背景のかげでしばし泣き合った』というのです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "The last bit has a good swing to it, eh," the near-sighted man said to them all.
curious.ja: 「最後のところはなかなか振ってる、ね」と、近眼は皆に向って言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That without it the whole piece goes slack shows," the knowledge-face man put in, "how feeble a thing this story is, don't you think?"
curious.ja: 「それがなければ全篇が引きたたないのをみても」と、知識がおもつけ加えた、「この小説があまりに心細い出来であることが分ると思いますが――？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's it, eh," the host answered as if the strength had gone out of his shoulders. "In the end it isn't much of a piece."
curious.ja: 「そうだ、ね」主人は、もう肩が抜けたというような返事であった。「結局、そうたいした作ではない」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Nekohachi made a show of opening his eyes wide, as if thunderstruck, when he came to hear of this last business of weeping together. He could not say he did not know himself that this too was a face put on and exaggerated on purpose, and yet at the same time, before he knew it, what was always kept hidden in the bottom of his heart seemed to have come out upon his face, for the grief over his own trade and the wavering over whether to make his second son into a second Nekohachi had been coaxed out together at once. He tried not to show people a face so ill-suited to his comic trade, but the harder he tried the less the face itself would obey him, quite the other way, and if he saw it in a mirror he thought it must look like a blubbering face. But without patching it up any more, plainly, "Well, I am impressed," he showed his respect as if the story were the very work of the company present. "I've got the same sort of sorrow myself, and it truly struck home, it did, eh. But if I too may be allowed the one, what you gentlemen would call a criticism, this Fukai playing a part against his own wish and letting his child see it, that I think was a grave mistake, eh?"
curious.ja: 「………」猫八はそれでもこの最後の泣き合いの一件を聴くにいたってびッくり仰天をしたほどに目を見張ってみせた。これもやはりわざと誇張してみせた表情だとは自分ながら知らないでもなかったが、同時にわれ知らず、いつもは心の奥にのみ秘めていた物が顔にまで現われた気がしたというのは、自分の職業に対する悲しみと次男を第二の猫八にさせようかどうかという惑いとが一ときに誘いだされたからである。彼は自分の滑稽商売にも似合わぬ顔つきを人には見せたくないと努めているのだが、努めれば努めるほど顔その物が反対に言うことをきかなくなって、鏡にでも映してみれば、自分の顔がべそ掻き面になってるように思われた。が、もう、それを取り繕うことをしないで素直に、「いや感心いたしました」と、その小説が一座の作その物ででもあるかのように敬意を表した。「わたくしにも同じような悲哀がございまして、いかにも感心いたしました。けれども、もしわたくしにも、その、先生方のおしになる批評と申すのを一つ言わせていただきますと、その深井というのが自分の本意でない役を演じながら、それを子供に見せておいたのははなはだしい間違いだと思われますが――？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's neither here nor there, it's no question for the author."
curious.ja: 「そりゃアどうでもえいことで、作者としては問題でない」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But with me it won't do to let it go at that," he said, hitching himself forward a little on his knees as if he were well and truly joining the debate now, standing up to the Tenjin-sama man. "I've got children myself, you see, my eldest and my second boy go to grade school, and the second, the twelve-year-old, when it comes to copying me he's a genius, so if I'm out sick from my seat he says he'll go in Dad's place, eh"
curious.ja: 「ところが、わたくしにはどうでもいいわけに行かないのです」と、彼は自分もいよいよ討論会の仲間入りをでもしているかのごとく少し膝をにじりだして、天神さまの意見に反対するのであった。「わたくしにも子供がごぜいまして、総領と次男とは小学へ通ってますが、次男の十二になるのがわたくしの真似にかけちゃア天才で、わたくしが病気ででも席を欠勤いたしますと、お父アんの代りに行ってやろうなんて申します」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Ha, ha," the Tenjin-sama man laughed, in a laugh half as if impressed and half as if making fun.
curious.ja: 「は、はア」と、天神さまは感心したような、またばかにしたような笑い方をした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Trade it may be, but with the old man already doing fool tricks, I don't want the child laughed at too, so to keep the children from coming near the yose where their dad appears I've gone out of my way to live in this awkward suburb on purpose, eh"
curious.ja: 「商売とは申しながら、たださえおやじがばかな真似をしておりますのに、わたくしはまた子供までばかにされたくないので、子供がおやじの出る寄席へ接近しないため、わざわざこんな不便な郊外にも住んでるのでげすから、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Something of that sort of feeling does come out in it, too," the host answered him, "but that is not all the story is about, so this is fine as it is, I suppose."
curious.ja: 「そういう方の気分も多少は出ていないことはないが」と、主人は答えてくれた、「そこをばかり主とした作ではないから、これはこれでいいのでしょう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Don't you despise your own art too much, Nekohachi-kun?" the near-sighted man put the question to him like that.
curious.ja: 「猫八君は自分の芸をあまりばかにしてはいませんか？」近眼がこう自分に質問した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Of course," he stuck for a moment, but there was no need to think it over. "There's nothing else for it, eh. Human as I am, such as I am, I've got to make even a tiger's cry to eat my rice, eh"
curious.ja: 「むろん」ちょッと行き詰ったが、そう考えなおすまでもなかった。「そうよりしようがございませんから、な。いやしくも人間でありながら、虎の啼き声までして飯を喰わにゃアならないのでげすから」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But," the other went on, "unlike you, the hero of this piece always takes his child along to the theatre so he can become a performer all the sooner, doesn't he?"
curious.ja: 「けれども」と、一方の言葉は続いた、「この作の主人公は君とは反対に、早く芸人になれるようにと子供をつねに劇場へ伴ってきているのでしょう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "There's plenty of fathers like that about, and that's the trouble." Nekohachi was none too pleased. A performer is human too, and yet there seemed to be no sympathy for him in this company. Hanging about in a place like this he would likely not get so much as a penny by way of thanks, he thought, and inwardly chanted Tō Enmei's "let me go home, come—come, let me go home." That set him straight. And as the night deepened outside the open second floor, along with his children what worried him most again was the seedlings in his plot.
curious.ja: 「そんなおやじが世間には多いので困ります」猫八は少からず不平であった。芸人だッて人間だのに、この席の人間には自分に対する同情がないとみえた。こんなところにぐずぐずしていたッて、一文の御礼さえ貰えないんだろうからという気になって、心で、陶淵明の「帰んなん、いざ――いざ、帰んなん」を唱えた。この方が自分を潔くしたのだ。そして明けッ放してある二階のそとに夜がだんだんふけて行くにしたがって、子供の事とともに自分の畑の苗の事がまた一番心配になってきた。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Tō Enmei is the Japanese name for the Chinese poet Tao Yuanming, whose famous poem declares his return home from office to the fields. Nekohachi chants the line inwardly as an excuse to want to leave.
notes.span: "let me go home, come—come, let me go home."

curious.ja: 四
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then came, "What sticks in my craw more than any of that," and he wanted to say here was the Tenjin-sama fellow off on his chatter again, only it kept the same earnest tone as ever, "is this author's flippant attitude. An anonymous monthly review in the Jiji Shinpō abused this piece roundly, saying Kume must be a hopeless fellow to rest satisfied with anything so shallow, so I read it myself in earnest to see how shallow a thing it could be, and to me it did not seem anything to sneer at. But when I asked our host here tonight, it seems that reviewer is Kume himself."
curious.ja: そこへ、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「そんなことよりも、僕が一番癪に障ったのは」と来たので、また天神さまのお喋舌かと言ってやりたかったが、さきは例の熱心な調子であった、「この作者の軽薄な態度である。時事新報に出た匿名の月評にこの作を非常に悪口言って、久米もこんな浅薄な物に満足している男だからだめだというようなことが書いてあったので、じつは、僕もほん気でどんなに浅薄な物だろうと思って読んでみたのですが、僕にはそうばかにした物でもないと思われた。ところが、今夜ここの御主人に伺ってみると、その月評子とはその久米自身であるそうです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Yes," Nekohachi meant to put in unwillingly enough, but without knowing it he was grinning. And just as he had thought, he took it that with this author the fall or conclusion of the piece had not come from his true intent, his real intent was to fool people. And he took to this Kume fellow all at once. "Isn't he a bit of a witty soul, like Sanba of old, eh?"
curious.ja: 「へい」と、猫八はしぶしぶ口を出したつもりであったが、われ知らずにたりと笑っていた。そしてやはり自分の考えどおり、この作者には、この作の落ちまたは結論は自分の本意に出たのでなく、実際の本意は人をばかにした物だとうなずかれた。そして久米とかいう人ばかりをすッかり気に入ってしまった。「昔の三馬などのようにちょッとおもしろい人じゃアございませんか？」
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Sanba is Shikitei Sanba, an Edo comic writer famed for droll, teasing downtown voices. Nekohachi means it as praise from one performer to another.

curious.en: "He's not so flippant as all that, Kume as an author, eh," said the knowledge-face fellow.
curious.ja: 「そんなに軽薄なんか、なア、久米という作者は」と、知識がおが言った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "You can tell that from his work up till now, can't you?" That was the near-sighted man.
curious.ja: 「そりゃア、これまでの作を見ただけでも分ってるじゃないか？」これは近眼の言葉であった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "If he's a flippant man, it's only natural he makes flippant work. Whether to like it or dislike it is left to the reader's side."
curious.ja: 「もし軽薄な人なら、軽薄な作をするのが当り前で、――それを好いたり、嫌ったりするのは読者がわの勝手だろう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "So it's up to the customer, is it, eh," Nekohachi took the host's argument this way. And growing eager to cozy up to it, "But he's a man with a deal of teasing wit in him, and I think him a great man, eh?"
curious.ja: 「やはり、お客次第でげすか、な」猫八は主人の説をこう受け取った。そしてそれに嬌えこむ気になって、「しかしずいぶん茶気のある人で、わたくしは偉いと思いますが？――」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "There's great and great, you know."
curious.ja: 「偉いにも、いろいろあるから、ね」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Wa-ha, ha," two or three of them raised their voices together.
curious.ja: 「わはッ、はッ」と、二三名の者がいっしょに声を挙げた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Sensei," the student-like fellow who had not said a word till now spoke for the first time, his words carrying that nervous tone. "I've not read a thing of Mr Kume's, so I've no right to say anything about the man, but it seems to me a piece of fiction has no depth unless the author's personality is backing it, eh?"
curious.ja: 「先生」と、これまで一言も言わなかった書生らしい人が言葉にその神経質らしい口調を帯びさせながら、初めて口を出した。「わたくしは久米氏の物を一つも読んでおりませんから、あの人の事については何事も言う権利はございませんが、――創作にはどうもその作者の人物が裏づけられていないと深くないようにわたくしには思われますが――？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "You always talk like an idealist, but even the realists on the other side would never deny that."
curious.ja: 「君はいつも理想主義者的に物を言う人だが、いかにその反対のげんじつ主義者だッて、それはけっして否定しちゃアいません」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Then I feel easy about that, but..."
curious.ja: 「それなら、安心ですが――」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Only we don't come to a stop at the sort of thing you mean."
curious.ja: 「ただ君の言うようなことにばかり僕らは停止してはいない」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's just what I can't..." the other said, cocking his head a little to one side.
curious.ja: 「そこがどうも」と、一方は小首を傾げた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Even if the man's character comes out, unless a life of that character comes out with it, it still won't be concrete, will it?"
curious.ja: 「たとえその人の人格が出たとて、その人格的生活が出ていなけりゃアやッぱりぐたい的にはならないではないか？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" The nervous student smiled now and made his bow. "Then even I can understand that."
curious.ja: 「………」書生の神経質は今度は微笑しながら、お辞儀をして、「それなら、わたくしにも分ります」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" He wanted to say, I haven't the least idea what any of it is about, eh. What they call *genjitsu-shugi* he didn't understand, and gutai and kuutai and that he didn't understand either, so he only thought of that konnyaku question-and-answer of the rakugo man.
curious.ja: 「………」わたくしにはちッとも何のことだか分りませんと猫八は言ってみたかった。げんじつ主義も自分には分らなければ、ぐたいとか空体とかも分らないので、ただかの落語家のこんにゃく問答を思いだしていた。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Konnyaku mondō is a rakugo routine of deliberately mismatched questions and answers that goes nowhere. Nekohachi thinks of it because the critical terms sound to him like pure noise.
notes.span: that konnyaku question-and-answer of the rakugo man

curious.en: In the meantime two or three more novels seemed to come up for discussion, but they did not take his interest the way the tiger had, so with his eyes on the Western picture he could make nothing of hanging on the wall to the right of where he sat and on the gilt lettering of the books in the bookcase knocked together out of beer crates to his front left, he bit back the yawns that kept coming. The host did say, We had better give Nekohachi some sake, but, "No, I am more for the katsubushi side," he answered, and had mochi cakes brought out by the host's wife. And as he talked with her about the pleasure of growing vegetables and about the bringing up of each other's children, he got two or three magazines the children looked likely to read.
curious.ja: その間に、なお二三の小説が問題になってるようであったが、虎ほどには自分の興味を引かないので自分の坐ってる右手の壁にかかってる訳の分らぬ西洋画や、自分の前方の左り手にあるビール箱で組みたてた書棚の本の金文字やらに目をやりながら、出ようとするあくびを噛みしめた。もっとも、主人は「猫八には酒を出すがよかろう」と言ってくれたけれども、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「いいえ、やッぱり、かつぶしの方が」と答えて、主人の細君に餅菓子を供えてもらった。そしてかの女とともに野菜作りの楽しみやお互の子供教育のことを語り合ったために、子供に読めそうな雑誌を二三冊貰った。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then from Takami-san, "Well, let us have you do something, eh."
curious.ja: そのうちに、高見さんから、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「じゃアひとつやってもらおうじゃアないか」と来た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" Now, from here on this was at last my world, he thought, and the damp feeling he had got from the tiger story went off somewhere, and he wanted them to think better of his art than of the tiger. He had righted himself before he knew it, and in his readiness there was the same braced spirit as on the kōza, and before he had yet done anything he could hear his own mimic voice. He bent the little finger of his right hand like a hook and started to carry it to his just opened mouth, then stopped and looked the finger over, half to himself, "Sweaty and short of oil, I wonder if it will go, eh."
curious.ja: 「………」さて、これからがいよいよおれの世界だと思うと、虎の小説に得た湿ッぽい気分などはどこへやら行ってしまって、自分の芸の評判を虎以上にしてもらいたかった。いつしか坐りなおしていた自分の用意には、高座におけると同様の引き締った精神が現われてまだやらぬうちから自分の物真似声が自分には聴こえていた。右の手の小指を鍵の手に曲げて、すぐ明いた口の中へ持って行きかけたが、ちょッと中止してその指を調べてみながら、半ば独り言のように、「汗で油切ってるから、うまく行くかどうか？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: After wiping the sweat off the finger once with his hand-towel, keeping his face deadpan, giving nothing away, he went hohokekyo.
curious.ja: いちおうその指のあせを手拭いで拭き取ってから、どこを風が吹くと言わぬばかりにして、ほうほけきょうとやった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "A fine thing, eh," Tenjin-sama blurted straight out in praise, but that jarred.
curious.ja: 「巧いものだ、なア」と、天神さまはいきなりこう賞めたのだが、それがうるさかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That just now was the nightingale in its cage, now the valley-crossing —" kekyo, kekyo, kekyo, hohokekyo! Then straight on the voices of the pine cricket, the bell cricket, the kutsuwamushi. Then crow, skylark, quail. With his joined lips pushed flat out to the front, the voice of the mole-cricket. Saying it might be a bother to the neighbours quieted to sleep by now, the male crane and the female crane told apart in the cry. The grass lark's voice too he let them hear.
curious.ja: 「今のは籠の中での鶯ですが、今度は谷わたり」けきょ、けきょ、けきょ、ほうほけきょう！　それから引き続いて松虫、鈴虫、轡虫の声。また、鴉、ひばり、うずら。合わせた唇を平たく前の方へ突きだして、おけらの声。寝静まったらしい近所へは少し迷惑だろうがと言って、雄鶴雌鶴の啼き分け。また草ひばりの声もきかせた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: To every cry, every cry, the listeners being listeners he could go all out, and they all seemed to be listening quietly, and it went as he wished and he was satisfied, and meaning for a bonus to show them the voice of the earthworm, "What they generally call an earthworm crying, that they say is the voice of the mole-cricket, but the earthworm cries too, eh," with that for a preface giving again a voice something like the mole-cricket, "If with this you do their voice you will see. For that study I once sat up all night in the wood at the Veterans' Home, but when footsteps sound, their voice breaks off for a while. I crouch there and wait a bit and then try it again, and if our voice is exactly like theirs, they answer straight off, and if it is wrong, there is no reply."
curious.ja: どの啼き声にも、啼き声にも、聴き手が聴き手だけにこちらが奮発できたので、皆も静かに耳を傾けた様子が見えて、自分の思いどおり自分も満足した、そしてお負けとして蚯蚓の声をしてみせるつもりで、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「一般に蚯蚓が啼くと申すのは、あれはおけらの声だそうですが、蚯蚓もやはり啼きます、な」こう前置きしてちッとまたおけらに似た声を出してから、「これで向うの声を出してみると分ります。わたくしはその研究に廃兵院の森で夜明かしをしたことがごぜいますが、人の足音がしますと、いったん向うの声が途切れます。そこへしゃがんでしばらく待っておりましてそれからまたやってみるのですが、こちらの声が向うのにそッくりだと、すぐ応じてきますし、間違ってると御返事がありません」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "ha, ha, ha!" The host let out a specially loud laugh.
curious.ja: 「は、は、はア！」主人は特別の高笑いをした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It's the truth, you know," he pleaded his seriousness. About the 'reply' — that was just his usual joke slipping out.
curious.ja: 「まったくですよ」と、自分はまじめを訴えた。御返事には、つい、いつもの冗談が出たにすぎないのだから。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Well, abroad there are men who have gone at it on a larger scale and have even studied the language of monkeys."
curious.ja: 「だから、さ、外国にはもッと大仕掛けに猿の言葉まで研究してみた人もある」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "If I ever get to learn English or something, I will try it myself, eh —"
curious.ja: 「わたくしも英語でも学んでおりますと、やってみますが――」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But monkeys do not use English."
curious.ja: 「しかし、猿は英語を使わない」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Wa ha, ha," two or three of them came out together.
curious.ja: 「わはッ、はッ」と、二三名。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" He felt quite as if his own stock in trade had been taken from him, and his spirits fell a little flat. Just to cover it, "They say on learned grounds that the monkey has turned into man, but in the story here the tiger has turned into a monkey, eh."
curious.ja: 「………」まるでお株を取られた気がして、ちょッと興ざめた。そのごまかしにだが、「学術上では、猿が人間に進化したと申すそうですが、ここのお話は虎が猿になりました」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, we are glad to have it in your animal mimicry too," the host answered.
curious.ja: 「いや、君の動物まね声にもなってありがたいよ」と、主人は答えた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 五
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That aside," the man with the face like Tenjin-sama, whom he had till now thought a disagreeable fellow, asked him a good question this time. "I want to hear your motive for coming to do such things, eh."
curious.ja: 「それはそうと」と、これまで厭な奴だと思われた天神さまが、この時いいことを尋ねてくれた。「君がそういうことをするようになった動機を聴きたい、ね」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Motive, you say —?"
curious.ja: 「動機と申しますと――？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Well, call it the first notion that started it."
curious.ja: 「まア、言ってみれば、初まりの思いつき、さ」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I see, eh — for all you see of me I wasn't a farmer from the first, no, nor any born artiste neither, though I daresay that goes for any of us, eh," he joked, and then he told of old days that held memories even for him. After one arm and one leg had gone useless he had talked it over with his wife and turned candy-seller. But just blowing the Chinese flute and hobbling along, hobbling along, not the snottiest-nosed brat would buy from him. The first day was clean zero and on the second day at last he sold ten sen's worth. He left that one silver coin with the child to please him with it, and child being child, he set it down on the bridge rail and went off to play, and in between another child took it. On the third day too he went out for trade because he went, but this was never going to do, he gave up hope, and stretched his legs out on the Yoshiwara embankment and sat there in a daze, thinking. "It was here I got a heaven-sent idea, and got in me the makings of the performer I would be one day, eh," and having got a small laugh from his hearers with that, he moved on to how he learned the cry of the frogs. "Before I knew it, any number of frogs were crying out in the paddies." As now, he showed how he had turned his eyes that way then, stuck his face a little sideways, and a good deal handier than when he had tried it that time, closing his hand as if round an egg and bringing his mouth to the hole at the top, he let out a little kuk kuk of a cry. "When I tried it myself, out of all those many frogs just six or seven turned round my way. I thought that strange and wondered a while, and then once more," he said, changing to a kak kak of a voice to show them, "when I tried it, this time all the frogs except those six or seven turned to face me, every one of them."
curious.ja: 「なるほど、な。――わたくしはこれでも初めから百姓、いや、ドン芸人じゃアございません。もっとも、どなたでもそうでしょうが」と洒落てから、自分にも思い出の多い昔を語った。自分は片手片足が利かなくなってから、女房とも相談して飴屋になった。が、ただ唐人笛を吹いてひょこりひょこり歩いてるのでは、どんな鼻垂れ小僧でも買ってくれようはずがなかった。最初の日はまるでゼロであったが、二日目にやッと十銭分だけ売れた。その銀貨一つを子供に喜ばせかたがた預けておいたら、子供のことだから、それを橋の欄干に置き棄てて遊んでる間に他の子供に取られてしまった。三日目にも商売に出たは出たものの、こんなことではとてもだめだと失望して、かの吉原土堤の上に足を投げだして、ぼんやり考えこんでいた。「ここでわたくしは天来の思想を得て、他日芸人になる素養ができましたのでげすが」と、ちょッと聴き手を笑わせてから、かわずの啼き声を覚えた話しに移った。「ふと、気がつきますと、田ン圃でかわずがたくさん啼いている」自分は今、目をその方に向けた時の様子をして、顔を少し横に突きだし、その時やってみたよりもずッと上手な具合いに、玉子なりに握った手のうえの方の穴へ自分の口を持って行き、ちょッとくッくッという啼き声をきかせ、「自分もやってみると、多くのかわずのうちから六七匹だけがこちらの方へ向きなおった。これは不思議だとしばらく考えておりましたが、今一遍」と言って、かッかッと言う声に改めてみせ、「やってみると、今度はその六七匹を除いたあとのかわずがすッかりこちらを向いた」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The truth was, he did not suppose it had gone quite so cleanly as all that, but there was no witness who had stood by and seen it at the time, so with an easy mind he made the story pretty. "And what I found was, the first way of crying was the females, and the one after was the males. And there were only six or seven males there, and all the rest were females."
curious.ja: じつはそうすッかりうまく行ったとは思われなかったのだが、その時そばに見ていた証人があるわけでもないから、安心して話を綺麗にしてしまった。「そして分りましたのですが、前の啼き方はめすで、あとのはおすです。そうしてそこにはおすが六七匹いただけで、あとは皆めすであったのです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Interesting!"
curious.ja: 「おもしろい！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "…" He had had the Tenjin-sama's praise, and his own delight welled up still more. "This was my first notion, eh," and then when he went to where the children gathered and showed them the mimicry, the candy sold better than you would think. And from the next day the frog candy-man was waited for wherever he went.
curious.ja: 「……」自分は天神様のお賞めにあずかって、いっそう自分の興も湧いてでた。「これがわたくしの思いつきでして」、それから子供の集まってるところへ行ってその真似をしてみせると、案外によく飴が売れた。そしてその翌日からはかわずの飴屋がどこへ行っても待ち設けられた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Sensei, candy is quite a paying thing, eh, with only five sen laid out it came to thirty sen, forty sen at the time."
curious.ja: 「先生、飴というものはなかなか儲かるものでげして、わずか五銭のもと手でその時三十銭から四十銭にはなりました」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "What made you give up such a good paying line, then?"
curious.ja: 「そんなにいい儲け口を止めてしまったのには？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Why, my hobby got too much for me, eh. Shall I say mimicking the cry of things was in me by nature? I mimic anything. No, whatever cries, if I cannot mimic it I study it till I can. Among my customers there are often orders like cry the firefly or cry the colic-worm, but that not even a genius beyond me could likely do. As for me, nowadays cats fighting and the cries of insects and birds have got common, and I cannot keep up unless I mimic aeroplanes and motorcars too."
curious.ja: 「そりゃア、わたくしの道楽が嵩じましたのです、な。わたくしには物の啼き声を真似るのが持ち前に備わってたとでも申すのでしょうか？　何でも真似ます。いや、すべて啼く物で真似ができなけりゃア、できるまで研究いたします。お客さまのうちにはよく螢を啼けとか、疝気の虫を啼けとかいう註文が出ますが、それはわたくし以上の天才にもおそらくできますまい。わたくしとしては、今じゃア、猫の喧嘩や虫、鳥の啼き声では平凡になって、飛行器や自動車の真似もしなけりゃア追ッつきません」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Why, there is carelessness in mimicry too," the host said, "and by that carelessness many things get vulgarised."
curious.ja: 「そりゃア、物真似にも油断があって」と、主人は言った、「その油断で多くのものは通俗化させられてしまう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "At that rate you will only throw yourself away and go downhill, won't you? Rather than that, why not talk just as you told your own history now, natural and without frills, even when you go to the yose. Wouldn't that be a good deal more natural and interesting?" said the Tenjin-sama-like man again.
curious.ja: 「そんなことでは君も」と、また天神さまが言った、「みすみす堕落するばかりじゃないか？　それよりも、いッそ、今君が自分の経歴を語ったような具合いに、自然で飾り気がなく、寄席へ行ってもそのとおりしゃべったらどうや？　その方がよほど自然でおもしろいやないか？」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I think that would be good too," the near-sighted man agreed.
curious.ja: 「僕もそれがいいと思う」と、近眼が賛成した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But my life is in making fools of the customers from up on the kōza and showing it, that is where it is."
curious.ja: 「しかし、わたくしのいのちは高座のうえからお客をばかにしてみせるところにあるのです」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's right, eh," said Takami-san, with his arms round both his knees, as if taking his side. "His offhand sarcasm and heckling when they come, why, they are a treat to hear."
curious.ja: 「そりゃそうだ、ね」高見さんは両の膝を両手で抱いていながら、こちらの味方らしく言った。「この人の臨機応変の皮肉や冷かしと来たら、ずいぶん痛快ですよ」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "In return, when I get to a certain point, I make my compromise and my concession, eh. There are times I even cry the firefly and the colic-worm for them. They are things that do not cry in any case, so it does not matter how I do it, see," and then putting on a sharp look, "You don't understand much yourself, eh, can a colic-worm cry? If that will not do for you, I've took your gate money already, so you can get off home quick — only that would be too bare, so at the end I let the other fellow save face too — but you don't want to go home halfway either, do you. Truth is, I don't want to send you home either — that is what I make of it."
curious.ja: 「その代り、こちらもまたあるところまで行くていと、妥協や譲歩をしておきます、な。螢や疝気の虫を啼いてみせることもございます。どうせ啼く物でないから、どういう風にでもかまわないわけでげすが」と、それからきッとした見えになり、「おめえさんもずいぶんわからねい、な、疝気の虫が啼けるかい？　それが不満足なら、どうせ、もう木戸銭は取ってあるのだから、とッとと帰ってもいいぞ――これだけではあまり殺風景になりますから、最後には向うにも花を持たせまして――だが、おめえさんだッても途中から帰りたくはなかろう。おいらもじつは帰したくねいんだ――てなことにしてしまいます」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I wonder if that is a kind of ochi too?" asked the near-sighted man, laughing.
curious.ja: 「それも一種の落ちだろうか、ね？」近眼が笑いながらの問いであった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That, I take it, is a kind of conclusion, eh." This was Nekohachi trying to take back what he felt he had fumbled a little earlier over the ending of the Tiger. "But then, when I get called to the princes and the like, why, gyagya-gya," and with that baring his teeth, goggling his eyes, screwing his face into something queer, he showed them cats at it fighting, and set them all off at once. But keeping a straight face himself, he went on, "It is not barnyard fowl, showing you cats kicking at each other is still hardly out of place. When the person before me is a lady, I can well hear the laugh from behind the fan where she hides her noble face. But at times, when I went up to Mr ___ for instance, I was told, they say you are good not only at mimicry but at rakugo too, let our guests hear something funny, so I declined. It is far too awesome for me, I cannot. But I was pressed, so perform a turn I did, perform one I did, and it is a strange thing, from the very start not a bit of it gets across. As we only know our own low-down society, of course the story falls there too. 'Oi, Hachi, are you there,' says I," and with that he showed hitching his backside and sitting on the step at the entrance, "from the first that does not get across what it is about, 'beranmei, bare-arsed you cannot hitch up, eh,' none of that ready wit gets across. Begging pardon for a rude thing to say, there is nothing to bite on, where there ought to come a roar they all sit prim."
curious.ja: 「やはり、一種の結論でしょう、な」これは猫八には先に虎のお終いでちょッと言い損ないをしたと思えた、その取り返しのつもりであった。「ところが、これが宮様がたなどへ招かれてまいりますていと、ぎゃぎゃぎゃアなんて」と、突然歯をむきだし、目を躍らせ、顔を珍妙にしがめて、猫の喧嘩する時の様子をしてみせ、皆を一度に吹きださしめた。が、自分はすまして、言葉を続けた、「庭鳥じゃアない、猫の蹴合いをお見せ申すにはまだ差し支えはございません。先様が御婦人である場合などには、やんごとなきお顔をお隠しになる扇の影からもそのお笑いがよく伺われます。が、時によりますと、――○○○様へあがった時などは、お前は物真似ばかりでなく、落語というものも巧みだそうだから、ひとつおもしろいのをお客さま方にお聴かせ申せと言われましたので、わたくしはお断りいたしました。とても畏れ多くてできません。けれども、たってと言われたので、一席願いましたことは願いましたが、――妙なもので、初手から少しもお分りになりません。どうせわたくしどもはわたくしどもの劣等な社会の事しか存じませんから、自然その話もそこへ落ちます。――おい、八公、いたか」と言って、尻を捲くって上り框へ腰かける様子をしてみせ、「これがそもそも何の事だか通じないのですから、――べらんめい裸じゃア尻は捲くれねいから、な、なんていう気を利かしたおもしろ味も通じません。失礼な申し分ではございますが、まったく張り合いがない、どッと来べきところをでも皆様がたはおすましになっておられます」
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The blanks are in the source: circles standing for names of noble houses and viscounts. Leaving them blank is itself good manners about great houses.
notes.span: when I went up to Mr ___ for instance,

curious.en: "It's because the way you live is clean different, you know."
curious.ja: 「そりゃ生活がまるで違ってるから、ね」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That would be it, eh." He thought these learned gents were different after all. What he had run up against himself in the flesh and still could not explain, they had made clear for him in a single word. Truly the life of the upper folk and the life of the likes of us is clean different. The way we live is as far apart as the moon and a soft-shell turtle.
curious.ja: 「そうでげしょう、な」彼はさすがに学問ある人の仲間は違うものだと考えられた。こちらが自分で実際に当ってきながら、しかも自分では説明しきれなかったことをも、彼らのうちではたッた一言で分らせてくれた。本統に上つ方と自分らとの生活がまるで違ってるのだ。暮し方に月と鼈との相違がある。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Thinking so, he had the back row-houses in mind. First the blacksmith, slow to get going, always getting shouted at by his mountain-goddess. Next the woman hairdresser, no telling how many men she has gone through. Next to her our own place, and next to that the tram conductor, clattering about while folk are still sound asleep and off out to his bell-ringing trade. And right at the dead end the blear-eyed lame clam-seller. In summer they are a near stark-naked society, but of the lot only our place is anything like human. The field work is only my spare-time work, but even so there is an ease there those gaunt craze-driven lot know nothing of. And the daikon and leaf greens I give away free to them at times. For all that we are born-and-bred Edokko who keep no overnight money, I born from a geisha's belly in a famous Asakusa restaurant, my wife first-bathed in Kanda upper water. And with that he wanted to show off a bit of what he knew before them all.
curious.ja: こう思って、自分は自分らの裏長屋の事を心に浮べていた。とッつきが怠けがちの鍛冶屋で、いつもその山の神に怒鳴られてる。その次ぎが女髪結いで、男が何人代ったか分らない。その隣りが自分の家で、そのまた次ぎには電車の車掌がいて、人のまだよく眠ってる時からがたッぴしやりだして、ちんちん屋の商売に出て行きゃアがる。そしてどん詰りには、目ッかちで跛足の蜆屋がいる。夏は皆ほとんど真ッ裸かの社会であるが、そのうちでも人間らしいのはまず自分のところばかりだ。百姓はほんの自分の片手間仕事だが、それでもそこにあのがりがり妄者どもの知らぬ余裕がある。そして大根や菜ッ葉をも時々は彼らにただ分配してやってる。これでも自分らは宵越しの金は持たぬちゃきちゃきの江戸ッ子で、自分は芸者の腹から浅草の有名な料理屋に生れ、女房も神田上水に産湯を使ったものだ。ついでに自分の見識を皆の前に披露したくなった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: There was a time a grand carriage stopped at the mouth of our row, you see. They must have known well enough how poor we lived, but, "Is this the house of the performer called Nekohachi?" "Yes," and I was a bit put to it by that. "Then is the master himself at home?" "Yes, the master has just gone to the bath and is out," hardly could I step out as the man himself in nothing but a loincloth, eh. "If you will wait a moment, I will go and call him directly," I said, and stepped outside for the moment. I gave my wife a wink, but she made an awkward face. I made as if to leave the house and slipped straight into the blacksmith's by the entrance, told his wife the story and got her to bring a kimono and sash, and putting on the look of a man just back from the bath, with a borrowed towel wetted with water and a soap box in hand, "Sorry to have kept you waiting, I am Nekohachi, what is your business?" Pupil and master with faces not a bit different, no wonder they found it strange. "In fact I have come from the ___ house, and just now your name came up there, and as you are said to do an amusing act you are to come at once, so I was told to come and fetch you," that is what he said.
curious.ja: 「ある時、わたくしの長屋の入り口に立派な馬車が停りました。どうせまずい生活をしているのは御承知であったでげしょうが、――猫八と申す芸人の家はこちらか？――へいと、わたくしはちょッと当惑いたしました。――では、本人は在宅かどうか？――へい、師匠は今湯にまいって留守ですが――まさか、ふんどし一つのわたくしがその本人ですとは出られませんから、な。――ちょッとお待ちを願います、ただ今すぐ呼んでまいりますから――と言ってひとまずそとへ出ました。女房にはちょッと目くばせいたしましたが、気まずい顔をしておりました。――わたくしは家を出るていと、すぐ入り口の鍛冶屋へはいり、そこのかみさんに訳を話して衣物と帯とを持ってきてもらいまして、今湯から帰ってきた風をして、借りた手拭いを水に濡らしたのと石鹸箱とを持って、――お待たせいたしました、すみません、わたくしが猫八ですが、御用は？――弟子と師匠とが少しも顔が違ってませんから、向うも不思議に思ったのは止むを得ません。――じつは、○○家から来たのだが、同家ではただ今お前の話が出て、おもしろい芸をする者だそうだからすぐ来るように言ってこいとのことだが、と言うのでした」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 六
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Just then the near-sighted man said he would be in a fix if it got any later, and stood up. Nekohachi looked up sidelong at that profile and showed a touch of displeasure, but the man never noticed. And on top of that two others stood up too, and went home together with him. If this were the yose, with the gate money already settled, it would be easier to give it up. But when a man has at last settled his heart and keeps on speaking straight, to walk out on him in the middle struck him as real rudeness, and he could not give it up. He wanted to tell them he would come out and haunt them from some dark alley on the way, but with the host among them there were eager listeners still left, so the thread of his talk was hardly broken.
curious.ja: この時、近眼があまり遅くなると困るからと言って席を立った。その横顔をじろりと見上げて、自分は少し不愉快の意を表したけれども、彼は気がつかなかった。その上に、また他の二人も立って、いっしょに帰って行ったのである。これが寄席なら、どうせ木戸銭はすんでるものだからという諦めもつきやすい。けれども人がせっかく心を落ちつけて正直に語り続けているその中途で失敬して行くのは、本統の失敬ではないかと思えて、諦めがつきかねた。途中の暗い横丁から化けてでてやるぞと言ってやりたかったが、主人を初め、まだ熱心な相手が残ってるので話の調子はさほど折れもしなかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "To come and fetch me at once just because my name happened to come up in talk, that is just like the nobility, eh. Even then, it is not that I will not go, you see, but with an Edokko temper, when they start with money straight off, I get contrary, eh."
curious.ja: 「今話が出たと言ってすぐ呼びに来るていなことはいかにも華族らしいです、な。そういう場合にでも、わたくしは行かないこともないのでげすが、――江戸ッ子の気性として、あたまから金のことを言われると、反抗心が起りまして、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But if it is business, there is no need for that, is there?" the host objected.
curious.ja: 「しかし商売なら、そんな必要はないじゃアないか」と、主人は反駁した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, business or no business, when they come at me squarely with how much will you come for, well, damn it, do as you please, is how I feel, eh. If it is a contribution then a contribution will do, and if they can pay then let them quietly pay what befits their station."
curious.ja: 「いや、いかに商売でも、四角張っていくらで来てくれるかと出られちゃア、もう、なに、くそッ、勝手にしろという気になります、な。寄附なら寄附でようごぜいますし、出せるならまた黙って身分相当に出せばいいでしょう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That old-fashioned stuff will never do. Better to ask beforehand, no coming unless it is so many yen and more, and an aristocrat, as an aristocrat, to pay far higher than a commoner, that nowadays is rather the sensible way."
curious.ja: 「そんな旧式なことアだめだよ。それよりゃア初めから何円以上でなけりゃア招かれない、そして貴族なら貴族のように平民よりもずッと高く出せと、前もって請求する方が今時はかえって見識だろう」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "But when money is named it turns dirty, eh."
curious.ja: 「しかし金銭のことを申すときたなくなりますから、な」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That's the old stale smell about performers today!"
curious.ja: 「それが今の芸人どもの旧臭味、さ！」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Performers today can't do any new tricks anyway, eh. If they don't come out to fetch you proper, why, I mostly turn them right down flat, eh. One time there I was, naked, lugging a hoe out in my plot, when a messenger from Viscount ___ came all the way to the field, and it got settled for such a day, from such an hour, but when he asks me how much will it take, I broke it off outright. A performer lives on spirit, eh, but then, if the fancy takes me, I'll go for nothing."
curious.ja: 「どうせ今の芸人にゃア新らしい真似などはできません。奇麗に出てこなけりゃア、おそらく、たいていぴッたり断りましょう。ある時など、わたくしがはだかで鍬を運んでますていと、畑のところまで○○子爵からのお使いがあって、いつ、何時からという約束になりましたが、いくらやればいいのだと聴かれたので断然止めてしまいました。芸人は意気で生きてますから、な――その代り、気が進めば、ただでも行ってやります」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That may not be a bad thing either, but then, what has become of this pig-farming Takami-kun means to start," so saying, the host turned the talk aside. And as if he knew quite well about things wholly apart from novels, talk that way went on a while among them all.
curious.ja: 「それも悪いことはなかろう――ところで、高見君のやりだそうという養豚の事はどうなりました」と言って、主人は話題を転じてしまった。そして小説とはまったく別なことをもよく知ってるかして、その方の話がしばらく皆とともに続いた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Just because I am here, no need to talk of nothing but animals, eh," he got the joke said, but he was already pretty well worn out. Likely because he had still not taken the supper he should take, and hunger was coming on.
curious.ja: 「わたくしが来ておりますからッて、そう動物の事をばかりお話になるにゃア及びますまい」と、洒落を言ったことは言ったが、自分は、もう、だいぶんに倦んでいた。取るべき晩食をまだ取らないので、腹がすいてきたにも由るのだろう。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The other guests were trading easy talk like how the trams had stopped anyway, but he wished they would all go home soon. And as his spirits sank, what strangely kept on his mind was the fee for tonight, if none comes then none will do, but whether it would come from Takami-san, or from the master here, or whether it would end just like this. Plenty here to chatter along with a professional like himself, but none that looked likely to have sense as listeners.
curious.ja: 「どうせ電車はなくなったのだから」というようなのんきなことをあとの客は語り合ってたが、自分は皆が早く引き上げればいいと思われた。そして気がめいってくると、不思議に気にばかりなったのは、今夜の謝礼を――出なければ出なくてもいいのだが――高見さんから出すのか、ここの主人からか？　それとも、このままになってしまうのか、ということだッた。本職の自分とともにお喋舌ばかりする奴らはいるが、聴き手としての気が利いていそうなものはなかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: He bore it, thinking it would be clear when this meeting broke up, which would be any moment now. But starting with Takami-san, no one considerately made a move, and to go dully home ahead of the rest would be dull too, so he took the host's wife again for company and talked of his own plot, what till now he had left forgotten. It was nothing he made trade of, particularly, but when talk turned to the plot, whoever he had for his listener, he at times grew so keen he forgot himself, and the spirit came back into him. This, as he had long thought, was his own taste, his pleasure. So,
curious.ja: この会が今にも解散する時には分ることだろうと辛抱しているのである。それにもかかわらず高見さんを始め、皆が思いやりなく動きもしないので、だからッてしかしぼんやりさきへ帰るのもつまらないので、自分はまた奥さんを相手に今までまだ忘れていた自分の畑の事を語った。別にこれは商売にしているものではないけれども、畑のことに話が向くと、どんな相手にだッても自分は時々われを忘れるほどにおもしろく、元気が出るのであった。これは自分としての趣味だ、楽しみだと、かねてから思ってる。で、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Eggplants, cucumbers, they'll be coming ready from here on, so whenever you have need I'll give you some," he said, covering over his own disagreeable face that would keep turning sullen. And the hand he had till now held back a little he put out three times running to the mochi cakes.
curious.ja: 「お茄子でも胡瓜でも、これからやがて取れるようになりますから、御入用の節はいつでもさしあげます」など言いながら、とかく不平そうになる自分の厭な顔を自分でまぎらしていた。そして前には少々さし控えられた手を餅菓子へ三度も続けてだした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 七
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It was close on one in the morning, when the cranes crying over at the Veterans' Home came through clear, and everyone got to their feet. He got to his feet too, brisk on purpose, and went down the stairs with the rest, but with the old magazines and the leftover cakes and senbei stuffed in his breast, if that was to take the place of tonight's thanks, it felt silly, and here in secret he wanted to hold that tiger close and cry a while somehow. It was not that he was fretting because he had got no money, that much he knew from the point of being an Edokko — and that too you would know if you saw how his wife, an Edokko herself, gave in to a woman's weak heart and now and then tried to save up overnight money, and he knocked her about till she spent it all — but set beside a farmer's working life, this body of his that had to show people worthless tricks to live on felt sad somehow, all over again.
curious.ja: 廃兵院で鶴の啼く声が澄みわたってよく聞える午前の一時近くになって、皆が席を立った。自分もわざと潔く立って、皆といっしょに二階を下りたが、ふところへねじこんだ古雑誌と菓子や煎餅の残物とが今夜のお礼代りかと思えば、ばかばかしいような気もして、ここでひそかに例の虎と抱き合ってしばらく何だか泣いてみたかった。けっして金の貰えないのをくよくよ思ってるわけでないのは、自分が江戸ッ子たる点に照り合わせても分ってるが、――そしてこれも江戸ッ子たる女房が、女の弱い気に負けて、時々よい越しの金を残そうとするのを、自分が投ぐりつけてまで使わせてしまうところを見てもらっても、分ってるが、――百姓の労働生活に比べてみると、自分は人にくだらない芸などを見せてそれで生活をしなければならぬ身が、今さらに何となく悲しかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It's only a little, you know—" Takami-san, who was not without thought for others, slipped him two yen coins in secret once they were outside, so he could pull himself together a little. And perhaps for that reason he could pay the more respect even to the host who came along behind saying to them all, "I'll see you partway, for a walk." But for himself — perhaps out of a nasty habit — what a stingy spirit, he thought himself mean. And if he could have it, he wanted to quit being a performer from tomorrow.
curious.ja: 「わずかだが、ね――」気が利かないでもなかった高見さんが、外へ出てから円助二枚をこッそり渡してくれたので、自分もちょッと気を取りなおすことができた。そしてそれがためにだろう、あとからついてきて、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.ja: 「散歩がてら送って行きます」と皆に言葉をかけた主人に対しても、いっそう敬意を払うことができた。が、自分ながら――いやな習慣から出たのだろうが――なんて、けちな根性だろうと卑しまれた。そしてなろうことなら、あすからでも芸人をやめたかった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: By now the only thing on his mind was the weather. Wondering when the rain would ever come, he looked up at the sky and hobbled along behind them all, hop hop, pitched to be heard by whoever he could not make out in the dim road,
curious.ja: 今や自分が気に懸るのは天気ばかりであった。いつ雨が降ってくれるのだろうと空を仰ぎみつつ、自分は皆の後からひょこりひょこり足を運んで行って、道が薄暗くて誰とも分らない人に聴こえるよう、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Tiger—monkey—pig, tonight it has been nothing but animal talk, eh."
curious.ja: 「虎――猿――豚、今夜はほんとに動物の話ばかり出ました」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "And your frogs besides," came the answer, and it was the knowledge-face man.
curious.ja: 「それに、君のかわず、さ」返事は知識がおのであった。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Thinking suddenly of the nervous one from the konnyaku question and answer, he could hear voices chatting away ahead with the Tenjin-sama fellow. Presently they passed the woods of the Veterans' Home, and in another step or two was the mouth of his own row house alley.
curious.ja: ふとこんにゃく問答の神経質を思いだすと、天神さまといっしょに前方を語り合って行く声がしている。やがて廃兵院の森を過ぎると、二三間で自分の長屋横丁の入り口なので、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "This back in here is where I live, it is a squalid hole, but if you are ever passing please step in," he said, taking his leave of them all. But he had one thing left he wanted to say, so he took one step forward and added, "And my plot, if you peep past the trifoliate orange hedge just there you will see it. It is dark now so you will not see well, but eggplants and cucumbers will be coming on plenty from now, more than the family alone can ever eat,"
curious.ja: 「この奥がわたくしの住居ですから、むさいところですけれども、もしお通りすがりにはお立ち寄りを願います」と言って、彼は皆に別れを告げた。が、今一つ自分としては言い残したことがあるので、足を一歩進めてつけ加えた、「それから、わたくしの畑はすぐそこの枳殻垣をお窺きになれば見えます。今は暗うございますから、よくはお見えにならないでしょうが、これからお茄子でも胡瓜でもずいぶんたくさんなります、家族だけではとても喰いきれないほどで――」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Well, gentlemen, I will take my leave here."
curious.ja: 「では、皆さん、わたくしはこれで失礼いたします」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The row house folk, who seemed already to be waiting even now for the eggplants and cucumbers to come, were all fast asleep. And the only one to greet this Edoya Nekohachi on his way home was the dog kept by the neighbourhood sake shop. But even to himself it seemed rare to be feeling so humble, and so human, as tonight.
curious.ja: 茄子や胡瓜のなるのを今から、もう待ってるらしい長屋のものらは、すべて寝静まっていた。そしてこの江戸屋猫八なる自分のお帰りに挨拶をしてくれたのは、近所の酒屋が飼ってる犬ばかりであった。が、今夜ほど謙遜な、そして人間らしい気持ちになってる時は自分でも珍らしいと思えた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The wooded road by the Veterans' Home was so dark that, for the sake of passers turning in from the tram street, he had petitioned some time ago to be allowed to put up a gas lamp with his own name written in it, for his own advertisement. The permission looked as if it would be hard to get, but that no longer mattered to him now. It only came to this, that nobody would needlessly give himself a stomach-ache over it.
curious.ja: 廃兵院は森道があまりに暗いので、電車通りから曲ってくる通行人のため、かねては自分の広告のために、自分の名を書き入れた瓦斯灯を立てさせてくれるように願いでてある。その許可が何だかむずかしそうだが、そんなことは、もう、どうでもよかった。誰れも無意義に自分の腹を痛めるものはないだけのことだ。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It did nag at him, after a fashion, that he had taken this overnight money with his stingy spirit, but whatever he might buy for them the children would surely be fast asleep by now. The toy shops and the food shops along the tram street would surely have their shutters closed too. So he would likely laugh it off as having got, the other way round, what he himself ought to have paid out in school fees.
curious.ja: ふと自分のけちな根性で受けたこの宵越しの金が気にならないでもないが、何を買ってやろうにも子供は、もう、熟睡しているに違いない。電車通りのおもちゃ屋や喰い物みせも、戸が締まってるに違いなかった。で、これも、自分で月謝を払うべきところで、あべこべにそれを貰ってきたことに笑いまぎらせてしまえるだろう。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: In any case, resolved to tell his wife at once the story from tonight's novel, and to make her taste it just as he had fully felt there an entertainer's sorrow, he drew near to the door of his own house.
curious.ja: とにかく、自分の女房にはさっそく今夜の小説の話をして、つくづく芸人の悲哀をそこに覚えたとおりかの女にも味わしめようと決心しながら、彼は自分の家の戸ぐちへ近づいた。
curious.label: house-checked

student.ja: 一
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Oi, boss," came the call, and Nekohachi lifted his eyes from the *Kōdan Club* he had been buried in and turned them toward the voice. He knew by the voice who it was, and that put him at his ease,
student.ja: 「おい、大将」と呼びかけられて、猫八は今まで熱心に読み耽ってた講談倶楽部から目をその方に転じた。その声ですぐその人だとは分ってたので、心易い気になって、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Well, Sensei!" putting on a vacant look on purpose. "Fancy meeting you on this tram, eh? So then, some fine nest has turned up round this way, eh?"
student.ja: 「いよう、先生！」わざと惚けた顔つきをしてみせながら、「よくこの電車でお目にかかるじゃアございませんか――さては、何かいい巣でもこッちの方にできました、な？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What, a Sugamo nest, that's all!"
student.ja: 「なアに、巣鴨の巣、さ！」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" That got him straight off, one down. But by now all the passengers around were pricking up their ears, so he called back into himself the feeling from the kōza he had just come off with his hands free. And with all the passengers starting to look like his own customers to him, he felt here he would have to give something back somehow. "That would be it, eh," putting on a suddenly solemn face, and just then with a sidelong glance catching their tram passing in front of the lunatic hospital he made it into material,
student.ja: 「………」それには彼もさっそく一本まいった。が、この時あたりの乗客どもがすべて聴き耳を立ててきたので、彼は今手が明いて引き上げてきた高座のうえの気分をまた自分の心に引きだしていた。そして乗客どもが皆自分のお客のように見えてきたので、ここはやッぱり何とかやり返してやらねばならぬような気になった。「そうでげしょう、な」と、にわかにもっともらしい顔になって、ちょうどこの時顛狂病院の前を自分らの電車が通ってるのをじろりと見て取って材料に入れた、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "In a place like Sugamo there is nothing living but madmen or monsters like Nekohachi, eh."
student.ja: 「巣鴨なんかにゃア、どうせ気違いか猫八のような化け物しか住んでおりませんから、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "ha, ha, ha," somebody laughed, and so even in a place like this he got the response he always got. He thought of the place and tried to hold back any further wisecracks on top of it, but somehow his mouth seemed unwilling to agree to it.
student.ja: 「は、は、はア」と笑った物があるので、彼はこんな場所ででもいつもの手応えを得るには得たが、場所柄を思ってそのうえの軽口をさし控えようとすると、何だかこの口が承知してくれないようにも思えた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Now, now, keep yourself quiet, eh," he was telling himself under his breath as he looked at the other's face. This was Takami, who had asked him along once or twice for some affair, and he was keeping that good-natured silent grin going on his sleepy face with a touch of drink in it. "Oi, little Buddha of little Nara" came right up to his throat, but he gulped it back down, thinking the man was no fellow performer to say that to. Then what looked like harmless words came rattling out. "Had your one already? This slump and all, Sensei looks to be doing pretty well for himself — let me have a bit of it, what do you say? Me, I'm off home now, if I'm lucky I might get something hot — though whether the missus has got it ready I don't know."
student.ja: 「まア、おとなしくしていなよ」ひそかに自分で自分を制しながら、相手の顔を見ていた。この人は高見といって、一二度ある催しに自分を招いてくれた人で、人のよさそうな黙笑をその少し酔いの出た、そして睡そうなあの顔に続けている。「おい、小奈良の小大仏」と喉まで出たが、朋輩の者でもない人にと思って、ぐッと呑みこんでしまった。それから、さし障りのないと思えた言葉がべらべらと飛びだした。「もう、一杯すみました、な――この不景気に先生はなかなか景気がよさそうじゃアございませんか？　少しあやかりてい、な、――えい？　わたくしなぞはこれから自宅へ帰って、やッと――その、な――熱いのにありつけるかと思ってますのでげすが、な、かかアがその用意をしてあるかどうかも分りません」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "ha, ha, ha!" The man holding his seat across the way and staring this way laughed again.
student.ja: 「は、は、はア！」筋向うに座を占めてこちらを見詰めていた男がまた笑った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: So long as he heard people laughing it rang pleasant in him, and yet it was strange that there was nothing funny to himself at all. If you wanted the comedian's logic for it, there was plenty and to spare. That to make people laugh there is no effect in laughing yourself is one of them. And yet, though he held off even from the drink people like, to protect this voice he uses for the trade, when he faced people he still had to make it look as if he drank. Could there be such hardship in any other work. People think a comedian just breezes along with no troubles in the world, but let them try being the man himself. He is thick with troubles people know nothing of. A man like himself is as if made out of a lump of trouble.
student.ja: 人の笑いさえ聞えれば、自分には気持ちよく響くのであるが、自分自身には少しもおもしろくないのが不思議であった。芸人としての理窟を言えば、それはたくさんあることはある。人を笑わせるには自分から笑っていては利き目がないということもその一つだ。けれども、自分は人の好む酒をもさし控えて、この商売に使う自分の声を保護しているくせに、人に向ってはやッぱり酒を呑むかのごとく見せかけなければならぬ。こんな苦しいことが他の仕事にもあろうか？　人は芸人なんてしゃアしゃアして、世に苦労もないように思ってるが、その本人にもなってみるがいい。人の知らない苦労をこてこてとしている。自分なんかはまるで苦労の固まりでもってできたような人間である。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Still, for one pleasure, he had pulled out the back fence of his row-house lodgings, and from there rented cheap from long back the open ground that lay beyond, and grew vegetables there. And when they came up plenty, not only did his own family eat them, he shared them out to the neighbours round about as well. Just to see the neighbours pleased was another pleasure in itself.
student.ja: それでも、一つ楽みなことには、自分の長屋住いのうら垣根をぶん抜いて、そこから出たところの明き地を前々から安く借りて、野菜を作っている。そして多くできた時は、自分の家族がそれを喰うばかりでなく、隣り近所のものにも分配してやる。近所のものが喜ぶのを見るだけでもまた一つの楽みである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The green caterpillars and black worms that get on the leaves of little turnips and daikon, you dig a ditch along the ridges, and shake the leaves toward it, and they all come rolling down. Then you stamp them all at once, or the children prod them with the end of a stick, and kill them.
student.ja: 小かぶや大根の葉につく青虫や黒虫は、畝並みに溝を掘っておいて、そこへ向って葉を振うと、皆ころころと落ちてしまう。それを一どきに踏みつけたり、子供なぞ棒の先で突ッついたりして、殺すのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Of late he had set out cucumber and eggplant seedlings as well, so the cutworms had to be watched. Like thieves, like us, the things do their work only by night, so hunt for them by day and you never see a sign of them. Tonight, he was thinking, the moment supper was done he would strip to his loincloth and have a child hold the lantern for him out in the field, and make a thorough job of doing for the cutworms.
student.ja: 昨今は胡瓜や茄子の苗をも植えつけたので、根切り虫に注意してやらねばならぬ。この虫は泥棒や自分たちと同様、夜業ばかりする奴だから、昼間探しても少しだッて姿を見せぬ。今夜はひとつ、晩飯をすませるとすぐ、自分はふんどし一つになり、子供に提灯を持たせて畑に行き、十分に根切り虫の退治をやってやろうと考えられた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Then the little-Buddha Sensei opened his eyes wide. "No more work tonight, I suppose?"
student.ja: すると、この時、小大仏の先生が目を見ひらいて、
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 「今夜は、もう、用がなかろう」と尋ねた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Yes, I have got my two kōza behind me, but —" That did not feel like answer enough, so catching what the other was driving at, "Might I tag along with you somewhere tasty, eh?"
student.ja: 「へい、高座は二個所すましてまいりましたが――」これでは自分の返事が足りないようにも思えたので、彼は向うの意味を汲み取って、「どこかうまいところへお伴できますか、な？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Oh, if it is only home to bed for you, why not come along with me?"
student.ja: 「なアに、どうせうちへ帰って寝るだけのことなら、どうだ、おれについてこないか？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "I will come — on your orders, anywhere." Even to Kegon Falls, the song says — the words came unbidden to his lips.
student.ja: 「まいりましょう――あなたのお指図なら、どこへでも」どこ、華厳の滝までもという歌を――思わず――口もとまで思い浮べた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It is a study group of writers, you know, no harm in listening a while. Come now and it is only two hours to stick out. Afterwards I will make it your world."
student.ja: 「ある文士たちの研究会だが、ね、聞いていてためにならないことでもない。これから行けば、もう、たッた二時間の辛抱だ。そのあとはお前の世界にしてやるから」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That sounds fun, eh, I'll come along too, to learn a thing or two, eh." He answered light enough, but he was fretting whether the load he had just set down would be loaded on his back again tonight. For him there was no time when body and mind felt lighter than in the tram on the way home after doing his union turn each night. From what he had heard he could not get home for at least another two or three hours. And in that time those cutworms might have cut through the roots of two or three of the seedlings in his plot, for all he knew.
student.ja: 「そりゃアおもしろいでしょう、な、わたくしも後学のためにお伴いたしましょう」そうは軽い気持ちで答えたけれども、今しがたやッと下してきた重荷を今夜また今一度背負わされはしないかということを案じられた。自分には、毎晩組合の義務を果して帰るさの電車の中ほど軽い身心になってる時はほかにないのである。聴いたところでは、今からなお少くとも二三時間は家に帰れない。してみると、その間にも畑の植えつけ苗の根を二本でも三本でもあの根切り虫に切られているかも分らないのだ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: With that worry on one side of his mind, the tram soon reached the terminus, so he stuffed the Kōdan Club inside his coat and got up after Takami-san, carrying his crippled body hobble hobble toward the exit. For a dozen years and more now his rheumatism had left him all but palsied down one side. Crippled as no one else is, he was thankful, as the saying goes that art saves the man, that he could still keep wife and children fed like anyone else.
student.ja: 一方にそれを気にしながらも、やがて電車が終点に着いたので、彼も講談倶楽部を懐中にねじこんで、高見さんの後から立ちあがり、ひょこりひょこりと、不自由なからだを出口の方へ運んだ。彼はこの十数年来リョウマチのために半身不随のようになってるのである。人並みならぬこんな身体をしていても、芸が身を助けるの諺で、妻子をまず人並に養って行けるのがありがたかった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Walking along in silence he was apt to sink into earnest thoughts like these, when a fat woman he knew met him and broke them up again.
student.ja: 黙って歩いてると、こんなきまじめな考えに沈みがちであるのを、ふと、知り合のでぶでぶ女に出会ってまたうち破られた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Nekohachi-san!" Pushing her fat bulk on ahead of her as if proud of it, she called out to him as they passed, though she need not have, in a gentle voice that did not match the bulk, "Home now?"
student.ja: 「猫八さん！」かの女はその太った図体を自慢そうに前の方へ運ばせながら、行き違いに、止せばいいのに、こちらへ、その図体にも似合わぬ優しい声をかけた、「今、お帰り？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Well, General Oyama!" He just had to tease again, so he teased as he always did. He turned sideways toward her and pulled himself up stiff and solemn to a stop, but she went off laughing, so he let her go out of his sight and chased her with words alone, "I've one more party to do yet, eh."
student.ja: 「いよう、大山大将！」彼はついまた冷かしてみたくなって、いつもどおり冷かした。横にその方へ向いてぎょうぎょうしく立ち停ったのだが、女が笑いながら行ってしまうので、自分の目を放して言葉でだけ追いかけさせた、「今一つお座敷があるので、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That's it," came the answer from behind. "You really are an earner!"
student.ja: 「そう」という返事は後ろに聴えていた。「ほんとにあなたは稼ぎ手よ！」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" Why, whether it would turn into money or not he didn't know, but with her carrying that body along as if to boast of it, he just wanted to boast of something himself, so he had called the place he was off to now a party.
student.ja: 「………」なアに、金になるのかどうかは分らないのであるが、向うがいかにも自慢げに見えるようにあのからだを運んでるので、こちらもただ何か自慢してやりたくなって、今からさして行く所をお座敷と言ってみたのだ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "A stout-built woman, eh," Takami-san said.
student.ja: 「でッぷりした女だ、な」と、高見さんは言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "How so — for all that, her husband dotes on her, so there's no standing against her, you know!"
student.ja: 「どうして――あれでなかなか亭主にゃア可愛がられておりますからたまりませんや！」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Takami-san was listening in earnest, but he himself knew nothing of the sort in fact. So long as it was a joke that was all he wanted. Thinking this man too was no great talker after all, he changed the subject.
student.ja: 高見さんはまじめに聴いていたが、自分にはじつはそんなことは分ってないのであった。ただ冗談でありさえしたらよかったのだ。この人も案外話せないと思いながら、話題を転じた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It's quite hot, isn't it, eh? At this rate will this rainy season be a dry rainy season, eh? That's trouble, eh."
student.ja: 「なかなか暑いじゃアございませんか？　この分じゃア、この梅雨は乾梅雨でげしょうか、な？　困ります、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Why, if it rains the feet coming to the yose will thin out, eh."
student.ja: 「そりゃア、雨が降れば寄席の客あしも減じようから、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "As for customers' feet, I'm seasoned to rubbing little sticks, you know. I've borrowed a bit of another man's ground and I'm growing vegetables. The trouble is that, if the rain doesn't come when it should, they won't do right, eh."
student.ja: 「お客の足なら、摺り小木にもなれでさア。わたくしはちッとばかり人の地面を借りて野菜を作っております。困るのアそれが、雨が降るべき時に降らないとうまく行きませんから、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 二
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Talking this over as they went, they turned in at the gate of a house. That even here a little patch of cucumbers had been made struck him as genteel.
student.ja: こんなことを語ってるうちに、ある家の門をはいった。ここにもわずかばかりだが胡瓜の畑を作ってあるのが彼には奥床しかった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: To get up to the second floor of that house he could only twist his backside up in a queer bobbing way. But when Takami introduced him to the party of six or seven with, "I've brought a rare guest along tonight. I thought we might have him do something for us later. This is the Nekohachi you've heard of," he felt the same pride as always when he cozies up to his customers.
student.ja: その家の二階へ上るにも、彼は変てこに尻をひょこひょこ曲げてでなければ上れなかった。けれども、自分の事を、
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 「今夜は珍らしいお客さんを一人連れてきた」と言って、高見さんが六七名の一座へ紹介してくれた時には、自分もいつもどおりお客に嬌えこんだ時のような誇りを感じた。「あとでひとつやってもらってもいいと思って――例の猫八です」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "This should be fun," somebody cried out.
student.ja: 「こりゃアおもしろかろう」と叫ぶものもあった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That 'the' I took to, eh, I'm a performer with a bit of a name myself, you know. So to come out before great literary gentlemen like yourselves, eh, and not feel stage fright like that, that's lucky for me." Saying this he glanced round the party. Some laughed innocently and none seemed to have taken offence, so he took them for people who would generously take his joke. But to make surer still, meaning to make them understand more, "Only let me tell you beforehand, with rheumatism my body doesn't work like other people's. So if I look to be sitting up stiff like this on purpose, that's why it is, eh, it's not exactly that I'm trembling before you gentlemen."
student.ja: 「例のは気に入りました、な、わたくしも多少は知られた芸人ですから。あなたがたのような偉い文士方の前へ出ましても、な、その、そうおじ気が出ないのは仕合せです」こう言ってじろりと一座を見わたすと、無邪気に笑ったものもあるし、別に感触を害しているようなものもないらしいので、こちらの洒落を皆寛大に理解してくれる人々だと分った。が、なお念のためにもッと分らせておくつもりで、「ただし前もってお断わりしておきますが、わたくしはリョウマチのために人様のようにはからだが利きません。したがって、こうわざと畏まってますように見えるのもそのためでげして、あながち諸君を怖がってるわけではございません」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "ha, ha, ha" came, so he felt safe for a start, and thinking they were his now he shut his mouth for a while.
student.ja: 「は、は、は」と来たので、彼はまず安心して、もう、こちらの物だとしばらく口をつぐんでしまった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: A study of somebody's novel had begun, but as the subject was actors, he pricked up his ears as a performer in something of the same line.
student.ja: 誰かの書いた小説の研究が初まってるのであったが、題目は俳優の事であるから、彼も縁の近い芸人として聞き耳を立てた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The man who looked to be the master of the house was someone he had often bathed with in the bathhouse two or three years ago and still met on the road now and then, and he said to Takami-san, "We are just now on 'Tiger.'"
student.ja: 当家の主人らしいのは、二三年前にはよく銭湯でいっしょになり、近ごろでも時々途中で出会うことがある人だが、これが高見さんに向って、
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 「今、『虎』が問題になってるところです」と言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Whose?"
student.ja: 「誰れのです？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "'Tiger' by Kume. It came out in the May Bunsho Sekai."
student.ja: 「久米氏の虎です、五月の文章世界に出た」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "I haven't read it," Takami-san answered.
student.ja: 「僕は読んでませんが」と、高見さんは答えた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Few here have read it either — and as the man who went out of his way to put it forward for the June meeting isn't here tonight, I was thinking of letting it pass without a word."
student.ja: 「ここにも読んでる人は少いのだが――これをわざわざ六月の会に持ちだしておいたその人が今夜出席していないので、何も言わないで通過してしまおうかと思ってるのです」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: To the question, "What sort of story is it?" the host answered, "I only glanced through it because he asked me by postcard to bring it up — thin if you call it thin, but neatly put together at its low level. The author can hardly have demanded much of himself, so for that author it will do well enough, I suppose — 'Tiger' is the part the hero, a comic actor, has been cast to play. To quote the original, this actor 'had a child already eight years old. And the child had trodden his first stage last year and had before him a future as a shinpa actor like him, no, more proper than him. He thought he would never make the child a comic.'"
student.ja: 「どんな筋なんでしょう」という問いに主人は答えて、
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 「僕もその人が問題にしてくれろと、ハガキで言ってきてあったのでちょッと読んでおいただけなのですが、――浅薄と言えば浅薄な物だが、低い程度で器用には纒まってると思う。作者にもそう深い要求がなかったのだろうから、あの作者としてはあれでもいいのでしょうが――虎とは作の主人公なる三枚目俳優が扮することになった役目です。この俳優には、原文を引くと、『もう、八歳になる子があった。そしてその子は去年初舞台を踏んで彼と同じく否、彼よりももッと正式な、新派俳優になる未来をもっていた。彼はその子をけっして三枚目にはしたくないと思った』」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" Hearing this reading, Nekohachi felt he had walked into an awful place. He knew himself that this was a bit of an overblown thought, and yet it sounded just as if they were talking about himself. He had four boys, the eldest fourteen in first year of higher primary, the next twelve in fifth year of elementary, both doing well and both monitors. This twelve year old was good at mimicking his father, and had an art even beyond his father's, but for all that he would not make him a second Nekohachi. No, it was just so as not to let the children see their father mimicking cat fights and animal voices and coaxing good humour out of the customers from up on the koza that he had long ago gone out of his way to choose this inconvenient suburb to live in. Cat turned to tiger, there was no great difference in that.
student.ja: 「………」この本読みを聴いて猫八はえらいところへ飛びこんできたものだと思われた。この思いは自分でも少しおおげさな考えだとは承知しながら、まるで自分の事を言われているようであった。自分には男の子が四人あって、総領は十四で高等一年、次ぎは十二で尋常五年、いずれも出来がよくて級長をしている。この十二のが父親の真似が上手で、しかも父親以上の芸を持ってるが、それでも第二の猫八にはしたくないのである。否、父親が猫の喧嘩や動物の声を真似して、高座のうえから客の機嫌を取ってるところを子供に見せたくないためにこそ、早くからわざわざこんな不便な郊外を選んで住んでるのだ。猫が虎に変っても、そこにたいした相違はない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "The part handed him was just the one part of the tiger." What the host was reading seemed to be the text of the story itself. "Not a man's name. Just the one part dressed up as a real beast of a tiger. He had even taken the byname of animal actor, so what wonder now to be handed the tiger to play. And yet he felt a little sad. Used to it as he long was, profession as he thought it, teasing as he knew it to be, he felt the human inside him being made a fool of, and even felt a little angry. The hero is in that sort of *situation*."
student.ja: 「彼の振られた役というのは、ただ虎の一役だッた」主人が読んでるのはその小説の本文らしかった。「人の名ではない。ほんとのけだ物の虎に扮する一役だけだッた。動物役者という異名をさえ取っていたので、今さら虎の役を振られたとて、それが何の不思議であろう。けれども、ちょッと悲しく感じた。長年馴れてきていながら、職業だと思っていながら、どうせ茶化しているのだとは思いながら、自分の中なる人間がばかにされてるような気がして、ちょッと腹立たしくさえ思ったというようなシチュエイションにある主人公です」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Quite deftly the point the author was aiming at holds together throughout," put in the man with the face like Tenjin-sama, in an earnest tone.
student.ja: 「なかなか器用には作者の狙ったところは一貫しています」と、天神さまみたような顔つきの人が熱心な口調で口を出した。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" The English word situation the host had just used stayed in Nekohachi's ears, and he took it to mean something like a painful fix you get caught in. And he himself was in fact fitted into his customers' favour, and had gone and fitted himself right into it, till he was in the state he was in now where he could move neither one way nor the other, so he joked it to himself, quiet. But down underneath he felt the hateful part of the performer's trade all the more.
student.ja: 「………」猫八には、今主人が言ったシチュエイションという英語が耳に残って、苦しいはめといったような意味の言葉ではないかしらんと想像された。そして自分は実際にお客様方の御贔負についはめられて、それに自分もついはまりこみ、とうとう二進も三進も動けない今の身分になってるのだとひそかに洒落れてみた。が、その心の奥ではますます芸人のいやなことを感じた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "There is the place where the leader points it out, eh, says that is just Fukai-kun's fitted part," said the priest-like one, close-cropped, with bumps rising fore and aft like a mountain range, the knowing face.
student.ja: 「座長がそりゃア深井君のはまり役だと指摘するところがあります、ね」と、五分刈りあたまの前後へむッくり山脈のできた善智識顔の坊さんらしいのが言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "And then they tell him the whole act will be eaten clean up by Fukai-kun's tiger, and such," the host went on, "and he got that much proud again even. But being the tiger, with no lines to say, there was no call to turn up for rehearsals even. Glad to make use of the day when the child begged to go to Ueno Zoo, he says, well then shall I show you the much talked of hippo, while in truth he means to go and study how a tiger looks. Then on the way, in the tram, he meets a theatre critic, and is asked where he is off to, so he answers, truth to tell, to the zoo to show the child the much talked of hippo, but the sharp critic has him marked, that is a lie, I have heard it already, it is the tiger really."
student.ja: 「それから他のものにもその幕はすッかり深井君の虎に喰われてしまうというようなことを言われて」と、主人は言葉を進めた、「彼はいくらかまた得意にさえなった。けれども、虎だから、台辞を言うことがないので稽古にも出る必要がない。その日を利用して子供は上野の動物園へ行ってくれろと言うのを幸い、じゃア近ごろ評判の河馬でも見せてやろうかと言って、その実、自分は虎の様子をでも研究してくるつもりになった。すると、途中、電車のうちである劇評家に出会い、どこへ行くのだと尋ねられたので、じつは、子供に大評判の河馬を見せに動物園までと答えたが、機敏な劇評家からそりゃア嘘だろう、もう聴いてるよ、じつは虎だろうと目星をさされた」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "There is a kind of sorrow comes out in a bit like that too," said the Tenjin-sama man.
student.ja: 「そういうところにも一種の悲哀は出ています」と、天神さまが言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" Nekohachi opened his eyes wide as if for the first time on hearing the word sorrow. It seemed to him more and more as if his own affair had been taken and remade and dug into. With his right hand stuck on the tatami and his left laid on the folded hand towel on his knee, admiring at how human feeling falls to the same place whoever feels it, he leaned his head a little back where he sat sideways and said, "I see! To an unlearned one like me a novel seemed a slapdash made-up thing with eight hundred lies strung together in it — though that may have been rude from the start to Sensei gentlemen like yourselves — but to hear it now, sure enough it aims at the true thing, it does, eh"
student.ja: 「………」猫八は悲哀という言葉を聴いて、今さらのように目を見張った。ますます自分のことでも作り換えて、うがってあるように思えたからである。右の手を畳に突いて、左りの手を膝の上にある畳んだ手拭いの上に置いてたのだが、人情というものは誰れが感じても結局こう同じところに落ちるのかと感心して、その横坐わりのままあたまを少し後ろへ反らせて「なるほど！　わたくしのような無学のものには小説なんかはいい加減に作り事を書いて、うそ八百を並べてあるものと思っておりましたが、――もっともこれはお歴々の先生方には初めから失礼であったかもしれませんが――今伺ってみますと、なるほど本統のことを狙ってあるものでげす、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Present-day novels are all like that, of course," the Tenjin-sama man answered, sounding a little angry. "We are different novelists from novelists who write lies and rest satisfied with it!"
student.ja: 「今の小説はむろん皆そうだよ」例のは少し怒ったように答えた。「うそを書いて満足している小説家とは吾々は小説家が違います！」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Fu, fun," went the knowledge-face man, laughing through his nose.
student.ja: 「ふ、ふん」と鼻で笑うのは智識がおであった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "How you do flare up," said the very near-sighted-looking man, smiling as he teased him.
student.ja: 「なかなか憤慨するじゃアありませんか」と、ひどい近眼らしい人もにッこりして冷かしを言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "I am not flaring up in particular, only there are plenty of fools in the world who take slapdash popular novels like Hekirurien's or Tokutomi Roka's for the fine standard and pass low, vulgar criticism."
student.ja: 「別に憤慨しているのではないけれど、世間にはよくばか者があって、碧瑠璃園や徳富蘆花のようないい加減な通俗小説をえい方の標準にして俗悪な批評をするものが多いから」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Terribly sorry, I am sure," Nekohachi said, keeping a straight face and dipping his head a little, and they all laughed. But this time that alone left him feeling unsatisfied, so he offered up one joke. "I for my part have never yet met a theatre critic in the course of my own researches, no, but once, to study the cry of the earthworm, I squatted up all night in the woods by the Veterans' Home over there, and they took me for a thief and a detective challenged me, he did, eh."
student.ja: 「どうもすみません」猫八はすました顔でちょッと頭を下げたので、皆が笑った。が、それだけでは今度は自分が満足できないような気になって、一つ冗談を言った。「わたくしは、しかし研究の途中でまだ劇評家にはお会いしたことがございませんが、ある時、蚯蚓の啼き声を研究するために、あの、そこの廃兵院の森に夜明しをしてしゃがんでおりましたら、泥棒と見誤られて刑事に誰何されたことがございます」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That too, you know, is the result of a kind of sorrow or earnestness," was all the explanation Tenjin-sama gave, and from no one else came any ha, ha, ha.
student.ja: 「それも、君、一種の悲哀かまじめかの結果だよ」という天神様の説明があっただけで、別に誰からも、は、は、はッとは来なかった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" Nekohachi felt the wind taken clean out of him, against all expectation. And for the first time it struck him that these were not his customers. As an entertainer he might make people cry or laugh, but he had no room left to cry or laugh himself. These people, though, were a cut above even that, for they seemed to study even the feeling of an entertainer himself who makes people cry or laugh and cannot cry or laugh himself. They were specialists in that line, right enough. At this rate an honest humility rose in him to take off his helmet cleanly and own himself beaten, and he asked, "And what did the actor do after that?" What he wanted to know most was about the child. All the same he had quite made up his mind the fall would be that he pleaded the part unworthy and did not go on the stage, or that at least he did not let the child come to the theatre.
student.ja: 「………」猫八は予期に反して、がッくり調子抜けがした。そして初めて思い及んだのであるが、これは自分のお客ではない。自分は芸人として人を泣かせたり笑わせたりしても、自分の泣いたり笑ったりする余地を持たない。ところが、この人々はまた自分らよりも一段うわ手で、人を泣かせたり笑わせたりする芸人その物の自分では泣いたり笑ったりできないその心持ちまでも研究しているらしい。さすがはその方の専門家たちだろう。これじゃア自分は潔く兜を脱ごうという正直な謙遜心を起して、「そうしてその俳優はそれからどういたしました」と尋ねてみた。おもに子供との関係を知りたかったのである。それでも、たぶん、役不足を言って舞台に出なかったとか、子供だけは芝居へ見に来させなかったとかいうのが落ちだろうとたかをくくっていた。
student.label: house-checked

student.ja: 三
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Just look. You've made a clean confession, haven't you, but if you want to see a tiger you needn't go all the way to the zoo — give anyone a litre or two and he'll turn into one, eh? — Why, shall we go and see that tiger over there? — That won't do. I can't shake this little one off, you see, and he looked back at the child again. There's a passage like that too," the host went on, still with an eye on the book. And everyone forgot Nekohachi and the rest and bent their hearts toward the tiger, but to Nekohachi that tiger was like himself. "For foolishness, Yui's part is much the same. Rather your single tiger part may be the honour, with the popularity gathering on the tiger alone, you know — thinking so I mean to do all I can with all my might, you know — Yes indeed, we for our part are rather counting on your tiger — Much obliged, and Fukai smiled wryly and yet was not a little comforted in his heart."
student.ja: 「そうれ見たまえ。みごとに白状に及んだじゃないかね、しかし虎を見たいんならわざわざ動物園まで行くにも及ぶまいぜ。――一二升飲ませれゃ誰だってなりますが？――どうだい、そッちの虎を見に行こうじゃないか？――そいつアいけません。何しろこいつを撒くわけには行きませんからね、と彼はまた子供をかえりみた。というところもあるのだが」と、主人はなお本を見い見い語って行った。そして皆が猫八などのいるのを忘れて虎の方へ心を傾けたが、猫八にはその虎が自分のようであった。「ばかさ加減を言えば由井の役だッて同じようなものさ。むしろ君の虎一役が名誉かもしれんぜ、人気が虎の一身に集まったりして、ね。――そう思ってわたくしも一生懸命やるだけはやるつもりなんですが、ね。――そうとも、僕たちだッてむしろ君の虎に期待しているよ。――恐れ入ります、と深井は苦笑をしながらも、内心少からず慰められた」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That won't do, eh," Nekohachi said, screwing up his face, "to do that situation in a place like that!"
student.ja: 「いけません、な」と、猫八は顔を顰めてみせながら、「そんなところで例のシチュエイションをやっては！」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "ufu, fu," a stylish little laugh was heard.
student.ja: 「うふ、ふ」と、乙な笑いが聞えた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Before gentlemen like you, for the likes of me to use cheeky English may have been a mistake —" He had thought better of it that this English might come to what they call compromise, but, "anyhow, if that actor they call Fukai lets the critic's puffing talk the decent human thought he had managed to hold in that case clean away, and goes carelessly getting into the swing again, that will be trouble, eh."
student.ja: 「先生がたの前で、わたくし風情が、生意気な英語の使い方をしたのは間違ってるか存じませんが――」この英語はいわゆる妥協ということに当るのではないかと思いなおしたのだが、「とにかく、その深井とかいう俳優がその場合にせっかく持った真人間らしい考えを、劇評家の煽てでなくさせてしまい、うかうかとまた調子づいて行っちゃア困ります、な」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "But that is just what makes it interesting, in a way —" the host said.
student.ja: 「ところが、そうであるからかえっておもしろくもあるのだが――」と、主人は言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "But as for me, a thing like that —" he said, turning earnest as if to show he was not fool enough for that, but neither the host nor any of the rest lent him an ear.
student.ja: 「しかしわたくしならそんなことは」と、彼は自分をそんなばかでもないと弁護するように熱心じみたが、主人ばかりでなく皆も耳をかたむけてくれなかった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "He went to the zoo and did no more than watch the tiger sitting still and yawning, and yet he came home thinking he had got the tiger's feelings better, somehow, than a handsome lover's feelings. When the first day came and the sewn-up tiger came onto the stage and yawned, at that alone there were cries of Fukai, Fukai! from the gallery, and he grew not a little proud. And at the fall of the curtain, when he leapt upon the heroine of the play, gallery first and the whole house with it gave him a great burst of applause."
student.ja: 「動物園に行って虎のじッとしているところや欠伸をしたのを見ただけでも、彼はとにかく色男の気持ちよりも虎の気持ちをよく分ったと思って帰宅した。いよいよ初日が来て、縫いぐるみの虎が舞台に出て欠伸をすると、それだけでも大向うから深井、深井！　と呼ぶ声がかかったので、すくなからず得意になった。そしてその幕切れのところで劇の女主人公に躍りかかると、大向うを初めとして諸見物の大喝采を得た」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Isn't that making fools of people?" It was the words of the much younger man, speaking for the first time.
student.ja: 「人をばかにしているじゃアありませんか？」これは初めて口に出すずッと若い人の言葉であった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That is making a fool of people, right enough," Tenjin-sama put in too, laughing this time.
student.ja: 「そりゃ人をばかにしたもの、さ」と、天神さまも今度は笑いながら口出しをした。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: A grudge rose in Nekohachi too about the way customers treat him on the kōza, enough to make him want to have his say. "From where I stand, it is the spectators he is making fools of, for getting delighted over trifles, and I daresay he is feeling for the actor himself, eh — spectators are the same as yose customers, you know."
student.ja: 「………」猫八もまた何か言ってみたくなったほど高座で受けるお客からの待遇に対する不平が浮んでいた。「そりゃア、わたくしから見ますと、つまらないことを嬉しがる見物人の事をばかにしているのでごぜいまして、たぶんその俳優の本人には同情していてくれてるのでげしょう、な――見物なんて、寄席のお客も同様でげすから」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Now, about that," Takami-san put in his first question with a mild look, "is it a work where the author is being ironical — I have not read a scrap of it, so I can hardly have an opinion — but to go by what I have just heard?"
student.ja: 「いったい、それは」と、高見さんは穏かな顔つきで初めて質問を出した、「作者が皮肉を言ってる作でしょうか――僕はさッぱり読んでいませんから、意見のあろうはずはないのですが、――今、聴いたところをもってみれば？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It is irony, to be sure," the knowledge-face man answered in a set-piece tone, "the question is whether the author can be satisfied with irony of so shallow a degree."
student.ja: 「皮肉には違いないのですが」と、知識がおが切り口上で答えた、「こんな浅薄な程度の皮肉でも作者が満足できるかどうかが問題でしょう」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That is it, I suppose." The near-sighted man spoke, for a near-sighted man, with unexpected crispness. "I have not read this one either, but what that lot write is all neatly put together in a small clever way, and without a scrap of *back* or depth."
student.ja: 「そこだろう、ね」近眼は近眼らしくもなく案外にはきはきした言葉であった。「僕もこれは読んでいないが、いったい、あアいう連中の書いてる物はいずれも小器用には纒まってるが、少しも背景や深みがない」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Just as Nekohachi-kun said," the knowledge-face man went on, "the author's sympathy for the hero is to be seen, but the way that sympathy is shown is exceedingly thin."
student.ja: 「今、猫八君も言われたとおり」と、知識がおは続けた、「主人公に対する作者の同情は見えてるが、その同情の現わし方がきわめて薄ッぺらなのです」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Thin or not, it is not that it has no background of life." That was the host. "Only, one may say he is an author who can give it no more than a thin background. As for T-kun going out of his way to propose this work, as he is not here tonight his true intent is unclear, but I take it he wanted to make a question for debate of the way it is both put together and yet somehow wanting."
student.ja: 「薄ッぺらでも生活背景がないことはない」これは主人の発言であった。「ただ薄ッぺらな背景しか持たせることのできない作者だと言えば言えるのだ。Ｔ君がこの作をわざわざ提議したのも、今夜出席していないからその真意は分らないけれども、たぶん、纒まってもいるし、またどこか物足りないしというようなところを疑問にして評議してみたかったのだろうと思われる」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "I daresay that is it."
student.ja: 「そりゃたぶんそうだろう」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Nekohachi wanted to make them all laugh by saying he did not know what the hell a *back* or a *haikei* was, but as what he had said had been taken up as a point he held his nose high and, with a solemn-looking face, "And so, is this novel finished with that, eh — is there no other fall to it?"
student.ja: 「………」猫八にはバックとかハイケイとかが何のヘラだか分りませんと言って、皆を笑わしてみたかったが、自分の言ったことを問題に採用してもらったので鼻を高くして、まじめくさった顔で、「そうして、この小説はそれでお終いでげしょうか――何か別に落ちでも？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: ha, ha, ha! Only two or three of them just laughed.
student.ja: 「は、は、はア！」二三名がただ笑うだけであった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: To Nekohachi it felt like the roar had come at a strange place.
student.ja: 「………」猫八には変なところでどッと来たものだと思われた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "You're no rakugo man," Tenjin-sama had stuck in another unasked word, or so it felt to Nekohachi, but he saw at once his own ignorance was being teased, so he buried his awkwardness in another apology.
student.ja: 「落語家じゃないよ」と、天神さまがまた入らざる口を出したと思われたが、猫八はすぐ自分の無学を冷かされたのだと分ったので、極りが悪いのをまた謝罪にまぎらせてしまった。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Yes, quite sorry about that."
student.ja: 「へい、どうもすみません」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "There is no ochi, no fall, in a novel, but what Nekohachi would take for a fall is what closes this story, and it is that which keeps the piece, thin as it is, alive. Fukai gets his great applause at the curtain and is going off proud in his sewn-up shape when from the shadow of the dark flats someone cries 'Father' and flings himself upon him. He looks back in surprise and finds his own child crying, child as he is, at the foolish part his father has played. He too cannot help crying, now at last. And then, 'the tiger and the human child wept together for a while in the shadow of the dark background,' that is how it ends."
student.ja: 「小説には落ちなんかはないが」と、主人は言葉を改めた、「猫八なら落ちともみるだろうと思われることがこの小説を結んでいて、しかもそれがためにこの一篇を浅薄ながら生かしているのだ。深井は幕切れに大喝采を得て縫いぐるみの姿で得意そうに引上げる時、暗い書き割りのかげから『お父さん』と言って自分に飛びついたものがある。びッくりして見返ると、自分の子供が父のあまりばかばかしい役をしたのを子供ながら泣いているのであった。自分も今さらのごとく泣かざるを得なかった。そして『虎と人間の子とは暗い背景のかげでしばし泣き合った』というのです」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "The last bit has a good swing to it, eh," the near-sighted man said to them all.
student.ja: 「最後のところはなかなか振ってる、ね」と、近眼は皆に向って言った。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That without it the whole piece goes slack shows," the knowledge-face man put in, "how feeble a thing this story is, don't you think?"
student.ja: 「それがなければ全篇が引きたたないのをみても」と、知識がおもつけ加えた、「この小説があまりに心細い出来であることが分ると思いますが――？」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That's it, eh," the host answered as if the strength had gone out of his shoulders. "In the end it isn't much of a piece."
student.ja: 「そうだ、ね」主人は、もう肩が抜けたというような返事であった。「結局、そうたいした作ではない」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "…" Nekohachi made a show of opening his eyes wide, as if thunderstruck, when he came to hear of this last business of weeping together. He could not say he did not know himself that this too was a face put on and exaggerated on purpose, and yet at the same time, before he knew it, what was always kept hidden in the bottom of his heart seemed to have come out upon his face, for the grief over his own trade and the wavering over whether to make his second son into a second Nekohachi had been coaxed out together at once.
